commands.name: port-feature

commands.name: port-request
commands.description: Port a request-specific change (C/C++ or similar source) from a local source codebase to a local target codebase through six approval-gated checkpoints (A diff the request, B trace it back into the latest source incl. renamed/moved code, feature extensions and data dependencies, C map to target with closure, D plan, E merge, F validate). Produces an auditable Before/After target snapshot, a single PORT_REPORT.md, and traceable work files. Use when the user wants to port/copy/apply a request (a Before/After change folder) from one codebase/model to another. (project)

commands.name: deep-research
commands.description: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. (dynamic workflow)

commands.name: design
commands.description: Grant or revoke Claude agent access to your Design projects

commands.name: design-sync
commands.description: Push a React design system to claude.ai/design. This runs a converter that bundles the real component code (from Storybook or a bare package) and uploads it. Use when the user runs /design-sync or says "sync my design system to Claude Design".

commands.name: dataviz
commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

commands.name: update-config
commands.description: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

commands.name: verify
commands.description: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.

commands.name: debug
commands.description: Enable debug logging for this session and help diagnose issues

commands.name: code-review
commands.description: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs (plus reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups where the model's recipe covers them) at the effort level given first, before any target (low|medium|high|xhigh|max: from few high-confidence findings to many, some uncertain); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply them to the working tree after the review. Pass --max-findings <n> to report up to n findings, or --max-findings all for every finding. The choice stays until you pass --max-findings default.

commands.name: simplify
commands.description: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.

commands.name: batch
commands.description: Research and plan a large-scale change, then execute it in parallel across 5–30 isolated worktree agents that each open a PR.

commands.name: fewer-permission-prompts
commands.description: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.

commands.name: doctor
commands.description: Health-check the user's Claude Code setup and fix issues: diagnose installation health — what the `claude doctor` terminal diagnostics cover — from local data (duplicate or leftover installs, PATH, unparseable settings files, broken or colliding agent definitions, skills whose frontmatter fails to parse); find unused skills, MCP servers, and plugins versus their context cost and disable dead weight; deduplicate local CLAUDE.md files against checked-in ones; trim checked-in CLAUDE.md files by cutting content a session could derive from the codebase (directory layouts, tech-stack lists, architecture overviews) while keeping gotchas, rationale, and non-standard conventions; migrate always-loaded CLAUDE.md guidance into lazy skills and nested CLAUDE.md files; flag slow hooks and context-heavy extensions; check the installed version is current; make auto mode the default permission mode; and pre-approve frequently denied read-only commands. Use when the user asks for a doctor run, checkup, audit, tune-up, or cleanup of their Claude Code setup or configuration.

commands.name: loop
commands.description: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace.

commands.name: schedule
commands.description: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule.

commands.name: claude-api
commands.description:
Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read FIRST, before you answer, run a command or open a file (already started? read it now); don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file; if nothing hits, load this skill).

commands.name: workflow-authoring
commands.description: Reference for writing a Workflow tool script (script API and gotchas, resume, quality patterns, worked examples). Load before authoring a script for a workflow the user already opted into; it does not itself authorize running one.

commands.name: run
commands.description: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

commands.name: run-skill-generator

commands.name: docs
commands.description: docs (editable docs people share and comment on; the default for any document, named as a doc or not: a document, report, proposal, resume, cover letter, letter, contract, policy, form, template, worksheet, essay, handbook, guide, how-to, cheat sheet, SOP or other writing to keep, share, collaborate on, send, submit, print or sign; a doc exports to Word, PDF, Markdown or Google Docs, so needing a file to send, attach, upload, submit or print is no reason to pick Word, and a file nobody asked for is a doc, not Word; a plan, comparison, summary or notes asked in chat stays in chat; a pasted claude.ai artifact link may be a doc: check with docs tools first; Word or another file format named, tracked changes wanted, or a .docx to change or use as a template → that format's skill): making one → if no docs-connector instructions are in context, call its `guide` (topic.instructions) first; then create the doc (headings only, no body) before any search, file read or plan, even with files attached. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: docx
commands.description: Use this skill whenever the user wants to create, read, edit, or manipulate Word documents (.docx) or Word templates (.dotx). Triggers include: any mention of Microsoft Word Documents, such as 'Word doc', 'word document', '.docx', '.dotx', 'microsoft doc'. Also use when extracting or reorganizing content from .docx or .dotx files, inserting or replacing images in documents, find-and-replace in Word files, working with tracked changes or comments, or converting content into a polished Word document. If the user asks for a deliverable as a Word or .docx file (to download, email or print), use this skill. However, if they ask for a document, page, report, memo, or notes WITHOUT naming a file format and the session offers Claude's own dedicated document or page skill or connector, use that instead, even if they will email or print it. Do NOT use for PDFs, spreadsheets, Google Docs, or coding unrelated to document generation. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: google-workspace
commands.description: Read this before the first Google Drive, Docs, Sheets or Slides connector call whenever the task creates or changes a Google file. Use this skill whenever the user wants to create or change a Google Doc, Sheet or Slides file in their Google Drive. Triggers include: a request that names Google Docs, Sheets, Slides or Drive and asks to make, edit, format, copy or rename a file; a docs.google.com link with a request to change that file, even a one-line fix or suggested edits; and any follow-up change to a Google file from earlier in the chat, even "change it" or "add a tab". Includes helper scripts for document positions, cell ranges and slide layout. However, if the user asks for a doc, deck or spreadsheet without naming Google, or gives a Google file only as source material for something new, use Claude's own output type instead. Do NOT use for read-only questions about a Google file, or for Word, Excel, PowerPoint or PDF files. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: import-memory
commands.description: Import a memory export from another AI assistant into Claude's memory — conversationally, additively, and with the content treated as data. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: morning
commands.description: Render the user's morning brief as a styled HTML artifact, or set it up as a recurring weekday task. Use only when the user explicitly asks to run, see, or set up their morning brief, or if they invoke /morning by name. A question about their day, schedule, or calendar is not by itself a request for the brief; answer it directly instead. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: pdf
commands.description: Use this skill whenever the user wants to do anything with PDF files. This includes reading or extracting text/tables from PDFs, combining or merging multiple PDFs into one, splitting PDFs apart, rotating pages, adding watermarks, creating new PDFs, filling PDF forms, encrypting/decrypting PDFs, extracting images, and OCR on scanned PDFs to make them searchable. If the user mentions a .pdf file or asks to produce one, use this skill. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: pptx
commands.description: Use this skill any time a .pptx or .potx file is involved in any way — as input, output, or both. This includes: creating slide decks, pitch decks, or presentations as PowerPoint (.pptx) files; reading, parsing, or extracting text from any .pptx or .potx file (even if the extracted content will be used elsewhere, like in an email, summary, or creating a different type of slide deck); editing, modifying, or updating existing presentations; combining or splitting slide files; working with templates (.potx), layouts, speaker notes, or comments. Trigger whenever the user asks for a PowerPoint or .pptx file, or references a .pptx or .potx filename, regardless of what they plan to do with the content afterward. However, when the user asks for a deck, slides, a slide deck, or a presentation without naming a file format, default to using a dedicated slide-deck artifact type or a separate slides skill if this session offers one; otherwise, use this skill. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: screen-item-definition
commands.description: 画面イメージ（モックアップ・スクリーンショット）から、システム化に必要な画面項目定義書をExcel形式で作成するスキル。1枚の画面イメージから単独の項目定義書を作成するモードと、変更前後2枚の画面イメージを比較して差分（追加/削除/変更/維持）を色分けした比較版項目定義書を作成するモードに対応する。ユーザーが「画面項目定義書」「項目定義」「画面定義書」「画面仕様」「変更前後の比較」「画面の差分」「UI項目をシステム化」などのキーワードや、入力フォルダにある画面イメージをもとに設計資料を作るよう依頼してきた場合は、このスキルを必ず使用すること。明示的に「項目定義書」と言われていなくても、画面イメージを基にエンジニア向けに項目を洗い出すような依頼には積極的に使うこと。 (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: skill-creator
commands.description: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: web-test-spec-creator
commands.description: Webサイトの検証表(テスト仕様書/テストケース一覧)を、検証観点表とテンプレートxlsxを元に作成する。検証観点はinputフォルダの検証観点表(xlsx)から、フォーマットはテンプレート(webテスト.xlsxなど)から、対象ページの仕様はソースコード・システム設計書・要件定義書・URLなどの追加インプットから読み取る。「検証表を作って」「テスト仕様書を作成して」「テストケースを起こして」「Webテストの観点表を埋めて」「検証項目を整理して」など、Webアプリ/サイトのテスト項目をxlsxとして出力したいときに必ず使うこと。コードや設計書がインプットされている場合は、それらから実際のフィールド名・バリデーションルール・ルーティング・画面遷移を読み取って具体的なテストケースに落とし込む。 (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: xlsx
commands.description: Use this skill any time a spreadsheet file is the primary input or output. This means any task where the user wants to: open, read, edit, or fix an existing .xlsx, .xlsm, .xltx, .csv, or .tsv file (e.g., adding columns, computing formulas, formatting, charting, cleaning messy data); create a new spreadsheet from scratch or from other data sources; or convert between tabular file formats. Trigger especially when the user references a spreadsheet file by name or path — even casually (like "the xlsx in my downloads") — and wants something done to it or produced from it. Also trigger for cleaning or restructuring messy tabular data files (malformed rows, misplaced headers, junk data) into proper spreadsheets. The deliverable must be a spreadsheet file. Do NOT trigger when the primary deliverable is a Word document, HTML report, standalone Python script, database pipeline, or Google Sheets API integration, even if tabular data is involved. (claude.ai sync)

commands.description: Turn the current work into a durable Notion page.

commands.name: claude.ai Notion:make-this-a-notion-database (MCP)
commands.description: Turn the current work into a trackable Notion database.

content.content:
# Glossary (authoritative definitions) | Term | Definition | |---|---| | **Request** | The change described by `SOURCE_REQUEST/Before/` → `SOURCE_REQUEST/After/`. | | **Formula** | A unit of source *behavior* changed by the request: a computation, condition, constant/threshold, table entry, setting default, or call sequence. The output folder name `formula-source-*` and the *Formula Mapping Matrix* refer to mapping these units from source to target. One formula usually corresponds to one or more changed symbols. | | **Hunk (`H###`)** | One `@@ ... @@` block of the source request diff. IDs are global across files, numbered in file order then hunk order. | | **Modification point** | One contiguous run of `-` and/or `+` lines inside a hunk, belonging to one symbol. A hunk that spans two symbols yields two points. Manifest = one row per (symbol, modification point). | | **Symbol** | Named code entity touched by a modification point. Kinds: `function`, `prototype`, `struct`, `union`, `enum`, `enum-const`, `typedef`, `macro`, `global`, `table` (initialized array/struct of entries, e.g. function-pointer registries), `preprocessor` (`#if/#ifdef` block), `file scope` (includes, pragmas, file-level comments). | | **Function column value** | ` ()`, e.g. `Density_Scale (function)`, `NvData (struct)`, `DENSITY_MAX (macro)`, `g_menu_table (table)`. Static duplicates: `is_valid@src/panel/menu.c (function)`. Non-code file: `N/A (non-code file)`. Unknown: `Not identified`. | | **Code file** | Extensions `.c .h .cc .cpp .cxx .hpp .hh .hxx .inc .ipp .s .S`. Everything else (Makefile, .mk, .txt, .xml, .json, .csv, binaries...) is a non-code file. | | **file_status** | `added` = only in After; `deleted` = only in Before; `modified` = in both and different; `unknown` = cannot be compared (binary, unreadable). | | **function_status** | `added` = symbol exists only on the After side of the file; `deleted` = only on the Before side; `modified` = on both sides; `unknown` = not identified or non-code. | | **Outside-diff dependency** | A symbol used by request code (added lines) that is not itself changed by the request (e.g. a callee, macro, type, header, config define). The target may lack it. | | **Incoming dependency** | Code outside the diff that uses a changed symbol: callers, registration tables, init sequences, NVRAM defaults. | | **Latest source** | `SOURCE_ROOT`: the current source. The request diff is the *seed*; the code actually ported comes from latest source. | | **Anchor result** (B) | Where a request file/symbol lives in latest source: `SAME_PATH` / `MOVED_FILE` / `SPLIT_FILE` (files); `SAME_NAME` / `MOVED_SYMBOL` / `RENAMED_SYMBOL` / `SPLIT_SYMBOL` / `MERGED_SYMBOL` (symbols); `MACRO_GENERATED` (name built by a macro); `REWRITTEN` (stable anchors still present, structure gone); `NOT_FOUND (removed|unknown)`. | | **Request link graph** (A7) | `_work/A_links.md`: nodes (request symbols and data items) and typed edges between them (`calls`, `declares`, `registers`, `indexes`, `localizes`, `defaults`, `reads`, `writes`, `includes`, `builds`, `guards`, `uses-external`), each proven by a `REQ-A:path:line`. | | **Node stability** | How likely a node's name survived later renames: `stable` (string literals/IDs, NVRAM keys, command keywords, build file names, guard macros), `medium` (types, fields, macros, tables, globals), `volatile` (functions, static helpers). B anchors stable nodes first. | | **Anchor propagation** | Using an already anchored node to find a linked one: read the anchored end in latest source at the spot that plays the edge's role (call site, table slot, prototype order…) – recipe R12 L1. | | **Link cross-check** | After both ends of an edge are anchored, the latest code must still show the relation under the latest names: `consistent` / `changed` / `broken`. | | **Search method / signal** | How an anchor was found and what supports it: `NAME`, `ALIAS`, `EDGE`, `NEIGHBOR`, `FUZZY` (R16), `ANCHOR` (stable literals/IDs), `SIM` + `SIG` (R17), `PATTERN` (rename rule), `LLM` (hypothesis, never evidence alone). | | **Fuzzy line match** (R16) | A request line searched as a regex where only feature identifiers are wildcards; finds lines whose callee/field names changed. | | **Rename-invariant similarity** (R17) | Token-shingle containment of a reference body in a candidate after replacing every non-keyword identifier by a placeholder; literals and structure kept. Deterministic, no embeddings. | | **Aliased request text** | REQ-A text with request names replaced by their latest names (`_work/B_aliased/`); used for latest state, hunk presence and evolution diffs so pure renames are not seen as changes. | | **Latest state** (B) | `UNCHANGED_IN_LATEST` (= REQ-A), `EVOLVED` (changed after the request), `REMOVED_IN_LATEST` (request lines gone). Per hunk: `PRESENT` / `PARTIAL` / `GONE`. | | **Evolution block** (B) | One change block between REQ-A body and latest body: `EXTENSION`, `BUGFIX`, `REFACTOR`, `UNRELATED`, `UNCLEAR` (rules: recipe R14). Drift = any `EVOLVED` item. | | **Feature extension** | Code added to latest source after the request that belongs to the feature: `EXTENSION` blocks inside request symbols, and `EXTENSION_NEW` symbols elsewhere (new S-ids marked `ext`). Ported together with the request. | | **Consumer** | Another feature in source that uses this feature. Never ported (`REPORT_ONLY`). | | **Port version** | What is merged to the target for a symbol: latest body limited to request lines + `EXTENSION`/`BUGFIX`/`REFACTOR` blocks (without `UNRELATED` blocks). | | **Data dependency** | Non-function item the feature needs: string/resource IDs and their per-language entries, enum entries and tables sized by them, settings fields + defaults + version/checksum, registry entries, config defines, data/resource files. | | **Alias map** | `_work/alias_map.md`: request name/path → latest source name/path → target name/path, with evidence. Used to compare bodies "modulo aliases" and to adapt ported identifiers. | | **Closure fixpoint** (C) | Dependencies are expanded repeatedly until no new item appears; a branch stops when the target already has it equal (modulo aliases). | | **Target state** (Checkpoint C) | `SAME_AS_SOURCE` (equals the port version, possibly modulo aliases → already ported), `SAME_AS_BEFORE` (equals REQ-B → clean base), `DIVERGED` (exists, differs from both), `SIGNATURE_DIFF` (different params/return/fields), `MISSING`, `RENAMED` (other name/file, ≥ Medium evidence), `RENAMED_CANDIDATE` (weak evidence). Comparison ignores whitespace only. | | **Confidence** | `High` = located by exact name and the bodies were compared; `Medium` = located but by partial match (different file, diverged body, anchor lines only); `Low` = inferred without direct evidence (rename candidates, naming similarity). For renames/moves the signal rules in recipe R12 apply (relation + content signal → High; 2 signals of different families → Medium; single or naming-only signal → Low). Every `Low` must appear in Blockers with a question. | | **Port class** (Checkpoint D) | See `decision-table.md`. | | **Target request-label convention** | An existing, consistent way the target marks request changes in code (e.g. `/* REQ-1234 */`, `// [CR#0123] start/end`). Applied only if found with evidence (≥3 consistent occurrences); otherwise `None found` and no labels are added. | | **Approval** | See SKILL.md §5. | # Checkpoint A – Source Request Snapshot Comparison **Goal:** an exact, complete inventory of what the request changed: files → hunks → modification points → symbols, with line-level before/after content. **Reads:** `SOURCE_REQUEST/Before/`, `SOURCE_REQUEST/After/` (and nothing else). **Writes:** `diffs/source/**`, `_work/A_files.txt`, `_work/A_ranges/**`, `_work/A_hunks.md`, `_work/A_links.md`, report section A. **Load:** `references/c-cpp-search-recipes.md` (R0, R1, R2, R15), `references/report-template.md`. ## Steps ### A1 – Prepare Set Workflow Status row A: `In progress`, approval `Not required`. Clear the Checkpoint A body (keep its sub-headings), delete old `diffs/source/` and `_work/A_*`. ### A2 – File list ```bash cd "$SOURCE_REQUEST" && diff -rq Before After ``` Normalise into `_work/A_files.txt` as `\t`: `Only in After…` → `added`; `Only in Before…` → `deleted`; `Files … differ` → `modified`. For `Only in` lines that name a **directory**, expand to every file below it (`find`). Exclude nothing silently: if you skip a file (e.g. `.DS_Store`), list it under Gate Result with the reason. Record per file: code/non-code (glossary), encoding (`file -I`), line endings (`file` shows CRLF). Whitespace/line-ending-only differences are still `modified`; note them as `cosmetic`. ### A3 – Per-file diff For each file run R0 and save to `diffs/source/.diff` (mirror the folder structure). Also keep the `-U0` output in mind for exact line numbers. Non-UTF-8 code files: diff the bytes as is, but read through `iconv` copies placed in `_work/` when you need to understand content. ### A4 – Symbol ranges For each code file run R1 on the Before side and the After side (when they exist); save to `_work/A_ranges/.before.txt` / `.after.txt`. Fix multi-line signatures by reading the lines above the reported header. ### A5 – Hunks, modification points, symbols For each hunk (in file order) assign `H001…`. Inside the hunk, split runs of changed lines into modification points; split again wherever the owning symbol changes. For each point: - `-` lines → owner from the **Before** ranges; `+` lines → owner from the **After** ranges. **Never take the owner from the text after `@@ … @@`**: git prints the nearest preceding function-like line, which is often wrong for tables/structs (e.g. it shows `Pjl_SetDuplex` for a change inside `g_pjl_table`). - Outside every range → classify with R2 patterns (`macro`, `prototype`, `global`, `enum-const`, `preprocessor`, `file scope`). If still unclear → `Not identified`. - `function_status`: owner exists on both sides → `modified`; only After → `added`; only Before → `deleted`; `Not identified` or non-code → `unknown`. - Static name present in several files → `name@path`. Write every point into `_work/A_hunks.md` (schema in `work-artifacts.md`). ### A6 – Line pairing (for `Line-Level Changes` and manifest cells) Within each modification point, take the `-` lines in order and the `+` lines in order, and pair them by position: the 1st `-` with the 1st `+`, the 2nd with the 2nd, and so on. If one side has more lines, put the extra lines on their own rows with the other cell blank. Never pair lines across points or hunks. Context (unchanged) lines are never shown. Prefix each cell with its line number: `L42: `. ### A7 – Request link graph (how the changed pieces connect) The hunks of one request are almost never independent. Record how they connect, **from the request alone** (REQ-A for added/modified items, REQ-B for deleted ones), so Checkpoint B can trace the easy, stable pieces first and then *walk the links* to the pieces that were renamed or moved (anchor propagation). Use recipe R15. Write `_work/A_links.md` (schema in `work-artifacts.md`). 1. **Nodes** – one per symbol owning a modification point (`A_hunks.md`), plus every data item the request adds or edits (string/resource ID, enum entry, settings/NVRAM field, config/guard macro, table entry) and every changed non-code file. Node id = `N###`; give its S-name, kind, `def at` (`REQ-A:path:line`) and H-ids. 2. **Stability** of each node (how likely its *name* survived later renames; B uses it as trace order): `stable` = string literals, string/resource IDs, NVRAM/settings keys, PJL/command keywords, enum values used as IDs, file names in build files, guard macros; `medium` = types, struct fields, macros, tables, globals, headers; `volatile` = functions and file-static helpers. When unsure choose the less stable class. 3. **Edges** `from –type→ to`, each with `REQ-A:path:line` of the line that proves it. One formula usually corresponds to one or more changed symbols. | | **Hunk (`H###`)** | One `@@ ... @@` block of the source request diff. IDs are global across files, numbered in file order then hunk order. | | **Modification point** | One contiguous run of `-` and/or `+` lines inside a hunk, belonging to one symbol. A hunk that spans two symbols yields two points. Manifest = one row per (symbol, modification point). | | **Symbol** | Named code entity touched by a modification point. Kinds: `function`, `prototype`, `struct`, `union`, `enum`, `enum-const`, `typedef`, `macro`, `global`, `table` (initialized array/struct of entries, e.g. function-pointer registries), `preprocessor` (`#if/#ifdef` block), `file scope` (includes, pragmas, file-level comments). | | **Function column value** | ` ()`, e.g. `Density_Scale (function)`, `NvData (struct)`, `DENSITY_MAX (macro)`, `g_menu_table (table)`. Everything else (Makefile, .mk, .txt, .xml, .json, .csv, binaries...) is a non-code file. | | **file_status** | `added` = only in After; `deleted` = only in Before; `modified` = in both and different; `unknown` = cannot be compared (binary, unreadable). | | **function_status** | `added` = symbol exists only on the After side of the file; `deleted` = only on the Before side; `modified` = on both sides; `unknown` = not identified or non-code. | | **Outside-diff dependency** | A symbol used by request code (added lines) that is not itself changed by the request (e.g. a callee, macro, type, header, config define). Node id = `N###`; give its S-name, kind, `def at` (`REQ-A:path:line`) and H-ids. 2. **Stability** of each node (how likely its *name* survived later renames; B uses it as trace order): `stable` = string literals, string/resource IDs, NVRAM/settings keys, PJL/command keywords, enum values used as IDs, file names in build files, guard macros; `medium` = types, struct fields, macros, tables, globals, headers; `volatile` = functions and file-static helpers. When unsure choose the less stable class. 3. **Edges** `from –type→ to`, each with `REQ-A:path:line` of the line that proves it. Types: `calls`, `declares` (prototype/extern ↔ definition), `registers` (table entry ↔ handler/ID), `indexes` (enum ↔ array or switch over it), `localizes` (string ID ↔ language table entry), `defaults` (settings field ↔ default/reset), `reads`/`writes` (function ↔ field/global), `includes`, `builds` (build file ↔ source file), `guards` (macro ↔ guarded block), `uses-external` (request symbol → unchanged symbol outside the request, e.g. a system API: such targets rarely change and become anchors in B). Endpoints outside the request are allowed (node kind `external`, def `outside request`). 4. Nodes with no edge at all → `isolated` (list them; B traces them only by content). 5. Components: group connected nodes (`C1`, `C2`…). Several components = the request touches several loosely related places; note it for the reviewer. ### A8 – Fill the report 1. `### Changed File Manifest`: one row per modification point, in `_work/A_hunks.md` order, `No` sequential. Repeat `file` and `function` for several points in the same symbol. Non-code files: one row per file with `N/A (non-code file)` | `unknown` | `N/A` | `N/A`. Column formats are in `report-template.md`. Write the `manifest No` back into `_work/A_hunks.md`. 2. `### Line-Level Changes`: per code file, the A6 pairs. 3. `### Request Links`: summary counts, then the graph and the edge table generated from `_work/A_links.md` (format in `report-template.md`): ```bash python3 -I "$SK/scripts/links_view.py" --links "$W/A_links.md" --out "$W/A_links.mmd" # paste its output ``` No `python3` → the summary and the edge table only (copy the edge rows of `A_links.md`). 4. Run `gates/A.md`, write `### Gate Result`, update Workflow Status (SKILL.md §4). ## Stop message ``` Checkpoint A . Files: (added a / modified m / deleted d, non-code k) · Hunks: · Manifest rows: Links: nodes (stable s / medium m / volatile v) · edges · components · isolated: Not identified: · Gate:

/ PASS Report: Reply "approve B" to start Checkpoint B (source change analysis). ``` # Gate A (all must PASS before status `Complete`) Write each result to `### Gate Result` as `PASS|FAIL – – `. 1. **File count** – number of files in `_work/A_files.txt` (after directory expansion, minus listed exclusions) == number of distinct `file` values in the manifest. Show both numbers. 2. **Diff files** – every changed file has `diffs/source/.diff` (non-empty). 3. **Hunk count** – `grep -c '^@@' diffs/source/**/*.diff` total == number of distinct H-ids in `_work/A_hunks.md`. 4. **Hunk coverage** – every H-id has ≥1 manifest row (`manifest No` filled); every manifest row of a code file traces to an H-id. 5. **Point coverage** – sum of `-` and `+` lines over all points == added/deleted line totals from `git diff --no-index --numstat Before After` (or the `diff -ruN` fallback in R0) for text files. 6. **Vocabulary** – `file_status` and `function_status` only `added|modified|deleted|unknown`; function values follow ` ()`, `N/A (non-code file)` or `Not identified`. 7. **Consistency** – `file_status=added` rows have `Modified_line_before = N/A`; `deleted` rows have `Modified_line_after = N/A`; non-code rows use `N/A (non-code file) | unknown | N/A | N/A`. 8. **Not identified** – each `Not identified` row has a reason in Gate Result (no silent unknowns). 9. **Template** – manifest header line equals the one in `references/report-template.md` exactly; rows numbered 1..n without gaps. 10. **Line-Level Changes** – one subsection per changed code file; no unchanged (context) lines; unmatched lines have a blank opposite cell. 11. **Link nodes** – every symbol owning a modification point and every added/edited data item is a node in `_work/A_links.md` with kind, stability and `def at` (show counts: owners in `A_hunks.md` vs nodes). 12. **Link evidence** – every edge has a `REQ-A:`/`REQ-B:` `path:line`; only the edge types of A7 are used. 13. **Isolated / components / view** – `isolated` nodes and the component list are written (or `none`); `### Request Links` has the summary, the Mermaid graph and the edge table generated from `_work/A_links.md` (edge rows in the report == edge rows in `A_links.md`), or the documented no-`python3` fallback. 14. **Inputs untouched** – no file was written outside `OUTPUT_ROOT` (`find "$SOURCE_REQUEST" -newer "$OUTPUT_ROOT/_work/.start_marker" -type f` prints nothing). 15. **Status row** – A = `Complete`, Next approval gate = `Awaiting Checkpoint B approval` (or `Blocked: …`). # Work artifacts (`OUTPUT_ROOT/_work/`) Markdown tables, one file per checkpoint. They are the hand-off between checkpoints: the next checkpoint reads these files instead of re-deriving. Keep them complete even when the report is concise. | File | Written by | Content | |---|---|---| | `input_baseline.txt` | Init | `shasum` of every file in `SOURCE_REQUEST/Before` and `After` | | `.start_marker` | Init | empty file; its mtime is the integrity reference | | `A_files.txt` | A | output of `diff -rq` normalised: `\t` | | `A_ranges/.{before,after}.txt` | A | top-level symbol ranges per code file (recipe R1) | | `A_hunks.md` | A | hunk + modification point inventory | | `A_links.md` | A | request link graph: nodes (stability) + edges with evidence | | `A_links.mmd` | A | Mermaid view of `A_links.md` (generated by `scripts/links_view.py`, pasted in the report) | | `B_links.mmd` | B | Mermaid view coloured by anchor result (`links_view.py --anchor`) | | `B_feature_ids.txt` | B | names of `medium`/`volatile` nodes, one per line (input of R16/R17) | | `B_aliased/` | B | REQ-A files with request names replaced by latest names (alias map applied) | | `B_anchor.md` | B | where each request file/node/symbol/hunk lives in latest source, method, signals, link cross-checks, iterations, latest state, evolution blocks | | `alias_map.md` | B, C | request name/path → latest source name/path → target name/path + method/evidence; rename patterns | | `B_symbols.md` | B | changed + extension symbols, port version, code/data dependencies, tests | | `C_trace.md` | C | target state per symbol + flows | | `D_plan.md` | D | mapping matrix + planned changes (full detail) | | `E_changes.md` | E | executed changes | | `F_validation.md` | F | raw command outputs (trimmed) + traceability | ## Schemas ### `A_hunks.md` ``` | H-id | file | hunk header | before range | after range | point | symbol (kind) | function_status | -lines | +lines | manifest No | ``` `point` = `p1`, `p2` … inside the hunk. `manifest No` = row number in the report manifest. ### `A_links.md` Nodes: ``` | N-id | name | kind | stability (stable/medium/volatile) | def at (REQ-A:path:line) | H-ids / S-id | component | ``` `kind` = glossary symbol kinds + `string-id`, `nv-field`, `config-macro`, `table-entry`, `build-file`, `external`. Edges: ``` | from (N-id) | type | to (N-id) | evidence (REQ-A:path:line) | ``` `type` = `calls`, `declares`, `registers`, `indexes`, `localizes`, `defaults`, `reads`, `writes`, `includes`, `builds`, `guards`, `uses-external`. Then `Isolated: ` and `Components: C1 = {N…}, …`. ### `B_anchor.md` ``` | id (file/N/S/H) | request location | latest location | anchor result | latest state | method | evidence (signals) | confidence | ``` Node rows use the A7 N-id as `id`; their `latest location` is `SRC:path:line ` (the name last, read by `scripts/links_view.py`). `method` = the rung that found it: `NAME`, `ALIAS`, `EDGE`, `NEIGHBOR`, `FUZZY`, `ANCHOR`, `SIM`, `PATTERN`, `LLM` (`LLM` = the lead came from a hypothesis; confidence still comes from the other signals). Link cross-checks: `| from | type | to | latest evidence (SRC:path:line) | result (consistent/changed/broken) |` Iteration log: `Iteration k: +n anchored (NAME a, EDGE e, …)`; not-found eliminations: `| N-id | checks run (L7) | conclusion |` Evolution blocks: `| S-id | block (SRC lines) | class (EXTENSION/BUGFIX/REFACTOR/UNRELATED/UNCLEAR) | R14 signals |` Extension hits: `| hit (SRC:path:line) | symbol | class (EXTENSION_NEW/CONSUMER/UNCLEAR) | reason |` ### `alias_map.md` ``` | kind (file/symbol/pattern) | request | latest source | target | method | evidence (R11/R12 signals) | confidence | ``` `pattern` rows hold a rename rule (e.g. `TonerSave_*` → `Eco_*`) with the anchored pairs that prove it. ### `B_symbols.md` Section 1 – changed symbols: ``` | S-id | symbol (kind) | file | H-ids | change type | behavior before → after | new tokens used | ``` `change type`: `new`, `logic`, `signature`, `constant`, `layout` (struct/enum member added/removed/reordered), `guard`, `registration`, `removed`, `cosmetic` (comments/whitespace only). Section 2 – dependencies: ``` | S-id | dir (out/in) | dependency (kind) | defined at (SRC:path:line) | in diff? | note | ``` Section 3 – port version: `| S-id | content source (SRC:path:lines) | includes blocks | excluded UNRELATED lines |` Section 3b – data dependencies: `| S-id | kind | item | places in source (SRC:path:line, all of them) |` Section 4 – tests: `| S-id | test file:line | covers |` or `none found (searched: )`. ### `C_trace.md` ``` | S-id | symbol | source location | target location | target state | evidence | confidence | note | ``` Plus flow chains: `FLOW-n source: SRC:a.c:10 Entry → SRC:b.c:42 Func → ...` and the matching `FLOW-n target: ...` (or `MISSING at `). Dependencies (from B section 2) also get a row with an `S-id.d#` id, e.g. `S003.d2`. ### `D_plan.md` Full Formula Mapping Matrix and Planned Changes (formats in `report-template.md`), plus for each P-id the exact text to insert/replace (fenced code), so E only executes. ### `E_changes.md` `| E-id | P-id | file | OUT-A lines | applied/skipped | note |` ## ID rules - Never reuse or renumber IDs after a checkpoint is `Complete`. - Every `S` names ≥1 `H`, or is `ext`, or is a dependency `S###.d#`; every `M` names ≥1 `S`; every `P` names one `M`; every `E` names one `P`. # Report template (the only authoritative copy) Create `PORT_REPORT.md` with exactly the content between the fences, then replace every checkpoint body placeholder with `Not started.` Headings, column names and status words must match character for character. Cell rules for all tables: escape `|` as `\|`; multi-line content joined with `
`; cell content max ~200 characters (truncate with `…` and point to the diff/work file); code in backticks. ```markdown # Port Request Report ## Run Metadata | Field | Value | |---|---| | SOURCE_ROOT | | | TARGET_ROOT | | | SOURCE_REQUEST | | | TARGET_REQUEST_ID | | | OUTPUT_PARENT | | | OUTPUT_ROOT | | | REPORT_PATH | | | Created at (UTC) | | ## Workflow Status | Checkpoint | Status | Approval to start | Next approval gate | |---|---|---|---| | A | Not started | Not required | Checkpoint B | | B | Not started | Not received | Checkpoint C | | C | Not started | Not received | Checkpoint D | | D | Not started | Not received | Checkpoint E | | E | Not started | Not received | Checkpoint F | | F | Not started | Not received | None | ## Checkpoint A - Source Request Snapshot Comparison ### Changed File Manifest | No | file | file_status | function | function_status | Modified_line_before | Modified_line_after | |---:|---|---|---|---|---|---| ### Line-Level Changes ### Request Links ### Gate Result ## Checkpoint B - Source Change Analysis ### Files Analyzed ### Latest Source Anchoring ### Changed Symbols and Behavior ### Dependencies and Test Coverage ### Blockers and Context Risk ### Gate Result ## Checkpoint C - Source/Target Flow Trace ### Source Behavior ### Target Behavior ### Gaps, Evidence, and Confidence ### Blockers ### Gate Result ## Checkpoint D - Formula Mapping and Plan ### Formula Mapping Matrix ### Target Request-Label Convention ### Planned Changes ### Validation Plan ### Risks ### Blockers ### Gate Result ## Checkpoint E - Before/After Implementation ### Output File Manifest ### Exact Changes ### Diff Summary ### Blockers ### Gate Result ## Checkpoint F - Validation and Handoff ### Validation Commands and Results ### Before/After Comparison ### Traceability Matrix ### Limitations and Tests Not Run ### Final Handoff ### Gate Result ``` ## Column formats **Changed File Manifest** (Checkpoint A) - `No`: 1, 2, 3 … sequential over the whole table. - `file`: repository-relative path in backticks. - `Modified_line_before` / `Modified_line_after`: `L[-L]: ` for that point's `-` lines / `+` lines. ≤3 lines: all lines joined by `
`; more: first 2 lines + `
… (+N lines, H###)`. `N/A` when that side has no lines (pure addition / pure deletion) and for non-code files. - If no file is confirmed: single row `| 1 | No confirmed files | unknown | N/A | unknown | N/A | N/A |`. **Line-Level Changes** (Checkpoint A): one `#### \`\`` subsection per changed code file, table: `| H-id | Modified_Before (-) | Modified_After (+) |` — one row per line pair (rule in `checkpoints/A-diff.md`), unchanged lines omitted, blank cell when a side has no counterpart. **Request Links** (Checkpoint A), three parts in this order: 1. Summary `| Item | Value |` rows: `Nodes` (`: stable s / medium m / volatile v`), `Edges by type` (`calls 4, registers 1, …`), `Components` (`C1: N001,N002,…`), `Isolated` (`` or `none`). 2. The Mermaid graph generated by `scripts/links_view.py` (```` ```mermaid ```` block + legend line), unedited. 3. The edge table generated by the same script: `| from | type | to | evidence |`. Rendering: VS Code with a Mermaid preview extension, GitHub/GitLab. Source of truth stays `_work/A_links.md`. **Anchored Link Graph** (Checkpoint B, `#### ` inside `### Latest Source Anchoring`): the same graph from `links_view.py --anchor`, each node with its latest name, anchor result, method and confidence; colours: green kept · blue renamed/moved · purple split/merged · orange Low · red not found/rewritten/removed · white not anchored. **Gate Result** (every checkpoint): one line per gate item: `PASS|FAIL – – `. **Formula Mapping Matrix** (D): `| M-id | Formula (source behavior) | S-ids / H-ids | Request location | Latest source location | Target location | Target state | Port class | P-ids | Confidence |` **Planned Changes** (D): `| P-id | Target file | Action | Anchor (exact target text or line) | Content source | Adaptation | Label |` **Output File Manifest** (E): `| File | Action (added/modified/deleted) | E-ids |` **Exact Changes** (E): `| E-id | P-id | File:lines (OUT-A) | Change | Status (applied/skipped + reason) |` **Traceability Matrix** (F): `| H-id | S-id | M-id | P-id | E-id | Output hunk | Result |`

content.content:
# Search recipes (C/C++ and similar)

Copy-paste commands. `$ROOT` = the root searched, `$S` = symbol name, `$F` = file, `$W` = `$OUTPUT_ROOT/_work`,
`$SK` = this skill's directory (scripts in `$SK/scripts/`, run with `python3 -I`).
Common grep options (define once per shell):
```bash
GOPT=(-rn --include='*.c' --include='*.h' --include='*.cc' --include='*.cpp' --include='*.cxx' \
      --include='*.hpp' --include='*.hh' --include='*.inc' --exclude-dir=.git --exclude-dir=build --exclude-dir=out)
```
macOS grep: `-w` is reliable; if `\b` misbehaves inside `-E`, use `-w` or `[[:<:]]` / `[[:>:]]`.
Always read results narrowly: `sed -n '<a>,<b>p' "$F"`.

## R0 – Diff of the request
```bash
cd "$SOURCE_REQUEST"
diff -rq Before After                                   # file list (Only in / differ)
git diff --no-index --no-color -U3 --function-context -- "Before/$P" "After/$P" > "$OUTPUT_ROOT/diffs/source/$P.diff"
git diff --no-index --no-color -U0 -- "Before/$P" "After/$P"     # exact changed line numbers
git diff --no-index --stat Before After                  # sanity count
```
For an added file use `/dev/null` as the Before side; for a deleted file `/dev/null` as After.
`git diff --no-index` works on plain folders (no repository needed) and exits 1 when files differ: not an error.
Binary: `git diff --no-index --numstat` shows `-  -` → `file_status` stays as computed, function `N/A (non-code file)`.

Fallback without `git` (same information, standard `diff`):
```bash
diff -u -p "Before/$P" "After/$P" > "$OUTPUT_ROOT/diffs/source/$P.diff"    # -N for added/deleted: diff -u -p -N
diff -U0 "Before/$P" "After/$P"                                            # exact changed line numbers
diff -ruN Before After | grep -E '^\+' | grep -vc '^+++ '                 # added lines total
diff -ruN Before After | grep -E '^-'  | grep -vc '^--- '                  # deleted lines total
```

## R1 – Top-level symbol ranges of a file (function / struct / enum / table bodies)
```bash
awk '
function trim(s){gsub(/^[ \t]+|[ \t]+$/,"",s);return s}
{ raw=$0; code=raw; sub(/\/\/.*/,"",code)
  o=gsub(/\{/,"{",code); c=gsub(/\}/,"}",code)
  if (depth==0 && o>0) { if (trim(code)!="{") {hdr=raw; hs=NR} else {hdr=prev; hs=prevNR} }
  depth+=o-c
  if (depth==0 && o+c>0 && hs) { printf "%d-%d\t%s\n", hs, NR, trim(hdr); hs=0 }
  if (depth==0 && trim(code)!="") { prev=raw; prevNR=NR } }' "$F"
```
Output `start-end<TAB>header`. A changed line inside a range belongs to that symbol.
Limitations – verify by reading the header lines when: the signature spans several lines (header
shows only the last line), braces appear in strings/`/* */` comments, or code sits in `#if 0`.
Lines outside every range: classify with R2 (`#define`, prototype, global, `#include` → file scope).

## R2 – Definitions
```bash
grep "${GOPT[@]}" -E "^[A-Za-z_][^;]*[^A-Za-z0-9_]$S[[:space:]]*\(" "$ROOT" | grep -v ';[[:space:]]*$'   # function definition
grep "${GOPT[@]}" -E "[^A-Za-z0-9_]$S[[:space:]]*\([^)]*\)?[[:space:]]*;" "$ROOT" | grep -v '=' # prototype
grep "${GOPT[@]}" -E "^[[:space:]]*#[[:space:]]*define[[:space:]]+$S([^A-Za-z0-9_]|$)" "$ROOT"     # macro
grep "${GOPT[@]}" -E "(struct|union|enum)[[:space:]]+$S([^A-Za-z0-9_]|$)" "$ROOT"                  # tag
grep "${GOPT[@]}" -E "^\}[[:space:]]*$S[[:space:]]*;|typedef[^;]*[^A-Za-z0-9_]$S[[:space:]]*;" "$ROOT"  # typedef
grep "${GOPT[@]}" -wE "$S[[:space:]]*(=[^=]|,|$)" "$ROOT"                                          # enum constant (check it is inside an enum)
grep "${GOPT[@]}" -E "^[A-Za-z_][^(]*[^A-Za-z0-9_]$S[[:space:]]*(\[[^]]*\])?[[:space:]]*(=|;)" "$ROOT"   # global / table
```
Static symbols may be defined in several files: always record the file and use `name@path`.

## R3 – Uses
```bash
grep "${GOPT[@]}" -w "$S" "$ROOT"                                  # every use
grep "${GOPT[@]}" -E "(^|[^A-Za-z0-9_])$S[[:space:]]*\(" "$ROOT"   # calls
grep "${GOPT[@]}" -w "$S" "$ROOT" | grep -vE "$S[[:space:]]*\("    # non-call uses: function pointers, registration tables, callbacks
```
Registration tables (menus, command tables, handler arrays, init lists) are the most common hidden
incoming dependency: for every non-call use, read the enclosing table (R1) and note the entry.

## R4 – New tokens introduced by the request (outgoing dependencies)
```bash
grep -h '^+' "$OUTPUT_ROOT"/diffs/source/*.diff | grep -v '^+++' \
 | sed -e 's://.*$::' -e 's:"[^"]*"::g' | grep -oE '[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*' | sort -u > "$OUTPUT_ROOT/_work/B_new_tokens.txt"
```
Remove C/C++ keywords and standard types/library names (`if for while return sizeof static const
unsigned int char void struct enum union typedef extern inline bool true false NULL uint8_t … memcpy printf …`).
**Follow only these tokens** (tokens the request adds). Do not walk whole shared tables or files that
the request merely touches – only the hunks are ported.

## R5 – Enclosing preprocessor conditions of line N
```bash
awk -v N="$N" '
/^[ \t]*#[ \t]*(if|ifdef|ifndef)/ { st[++d]=$0 }
/^[ \t]*#[ \t]*(elif|else)/        { st[d]=st[d]" / "$0 }
/^[ \t]*#[ \t]*endif/              { d-- }
NR==N { for(i=1;i<=d;i++) print st[i]; exit }' "$F"
```
For each macro `M` in the condition, check where it is enabled:
```bash
grep "${GOPT[@]}" --include='Makefile' --include='*.mk' --include='CMakeLists.txt' --include='*.cmake' \
     -E "#[[:space:]]*define[[:space:]]+$M([^A-Za-z0-9_]|$)|-D$M([^A-Za-z0-9_]|$)|$M[[:space:]]*[:+]?=" "$ROOT"
```

## R6 – Headers / includes
```bash
grep "${GOPT[@]}" -E '#[[:space:]]*include' "$F"                    # what a file includes
grep "${GOPT[@]}" -E "#[[:space:]]*include[[:space:]]*[<\"]([^>\"]*/)?$(basename "$H")[>\"]" "$ROOT"   # who includes header H
```

## R7 – Compare one symbol across trees
```bash
sed -n '<a>,<b>p' "$FILE_1" > "$OUTPUT_ROOT/_work/cmp_1.txt"
sed -n '<c>,<d>p' "$FILE_2" > "$OUTPUT_ROOT/_work/cmp_2.txt"
diff -w "$OUTPUT_ROOT/_work/cmp_1.txt" "$OUTPUT_ROOT/_work/cmp_2.txt" && echo SAME
```
Get the ranges with R1 on each file. Compare target vs `REQ-B` and target vs `REQ-A` to decide the
target state; compare `SRC` vs `REQ-A` for drift.

## R8 – Rename candidates (only when the name is MISSING in target)
Take 1–2 distinctive lines of the source body (string literals, unusual constants, unique call
sequences) and search for them in the target:
```bash
grep "${GOPT[@]}" -F '<distinctive literal>' "$TARGET_ROOT"
```
A hit is a `RENAMED_CANDIDATE` with confidence `Low` until the user confirms.

## R9 – Tests and build entry points
```bash
find "$ROOT" -type d \( -iname 'test*' -o -iname 'unittest*' -o -iname 'ut' \) -not -path '*/.git/*'
grep "${GOPT[@]}" -lw "$S" "$ROOT" | grep -iE 'test|_ut|spec'
ls "$ROOT" | grep -iE '^(Makefile|GNUmakefile|CMakeLists.txt|build.*\.(sh|bat|py)|.*\.sln|.*\.vcxproj|README.*)$'
```

## R10 – Request-label convention in target
```bash
grep "${GOPT[@]}" -E '(REQ|CR|PR|ECR|ECO|TICKET|ISSUE|BUG|FIX|MOD|CHG)[-_#: ]?[0-9]{2,}' "$TARGET_ROOT" | head -50
```
Accept a convention only if ≥3 occurrences share one format (prefix, comment style, start/end
markers). Record 3 examples as evidence.

## R11 – Relocate a file (moved / renamed / split)
`$P` = request-relative path, `$REF` = the reference file (REQ-A version for source anchoring, the source
version for target lookup), `$W` = `$OUTPUT_ROOT/_work`.
```bash
# a. same basename elsewhere
find "$ROOT" -type f -name "$(basename "$P")" -not -path '*/.git/*'
# b. includes: who includes the old header name / a header with the same symbols (R6) – a moved header is
#    usually still included by the same .c files under a new path
# c. content similarity: rank candidate files by shared normalized lines
norm(){ sed -e 's://.*$::' -e 's/^[[:space:]]*//' -e 's/[[:space:]]*$//' "$1" | grep -vE '^([{}();]*|/\*.*|\*.*)$' | sort -u; }
norm "$REF" > "$W/ref.lines"; total=$(wc -l < "$W/ref.lines")
grep -oE '[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]{6,}' "$REF" | sort | uniq -c | sort -n | head -15 | awk '{print $2}' > "$W/ref.ids"
grep "${GOPT[@]}" -lwF -f "$W/ref.ids" "$ROOT" | sed 's/:.*//' | sort -u | while read -r c; do
  n=$(norm "$c" | comm -12 - "$W/ref.lines" | wc -l); echo "$((100*n/total))% $c"; done | sort -rn | head -5
```
Relation signals for files (from `_work/A_links.md`): an anchored `.c` still `includes` a header at the same
place, or an anchored build file `builds` the candidate. File confidence follows the R12 rules with these as
relation signals and the similarity score as content signal.
Score ≥ 60 % → strong candidate; 30–60 % → candidate (maybe `SPLIT_FILE`: check whether 2 candidates together
cover the file); < 30 % → not the same file. The `ref.ids` are the *rarest* long identifiers of the file.
d. When the file's identifiers were renamed too (a–c find nothing): run R17 for the 2–3 largest blocks of `$REF`;
   the file that holds their top candidates is the file candidate (blocks landing in 2+ files → maybe `SPLIT_FILE`).

## R12 – Locate a symbol whose name is not found (search ladder)
`$OLD` = request name, body from REQ-A (from latest source when used for the target lookup in C).
`$W` = `$OUTPUT_ROOT/_work`, `$SK` = this skill's directory. Run the rungs **in order**; stop climbing as soon as
the confidence rules below give `High`, otherwise collect every candidate and its signals.
A missing name alone proves nothing: it may be a rename, a macro-generated name, a split/merge, a rewrite,
a removal or an encoding mismatch (L7 tells them apart).

**L0 – alias / wrapper** (signal `ALIAS`)
```bash
grep "${GOPT[@]}" -E "#[[:space:]]*define[[:space:]]+$OLD[[:space:](]" "$ROOT"
grep "${GOPT[@]}" -B2 -A6 -E "^[A-Za-z_].*[^A-Za-z0-9_]$OLD[[:space:]]*\(" "$ROOT" | grep -E 'return .*\('   # thin wrapper
grep "${GOPT[@]}" -w "$OLD" "$ROOT"     # also catches the old name left in comments ("renamed from …")
```
**L1 – walk the links** (signals `EDGE`, `NEIGHBOR`). For every edge of `$OLD` in `_work/A_links.md` whose other
end is already anchored in `$ROOT`, read that end's latest body and find the spot that played the edge's role:
| edge | where to look in the anchored end | the candidate is |
|---|---|---|
| `calls` (anchored caller → `$OLD`) | the caller's latest body; find the request call line with R16 | the function called at that position |
| `calls` (`$OLD` → anchored callee) | callers of the callee (R3) whose body matches `$OLD` (R16/R17) | that caller |
| `declares` | the header next to the anchored prototypes (same order) | the prototype in that slot |
| `registers` | the anchored table; entry with the same ID/key/slot | the handler/ID in that entry |
| `indexes` / `localizes` / `defaults` | the anchored enum, language table or default table; same position/value | the entry there |
| `reads` / `writes` | functions using the anchored field/global (R3) | the one whose body matches (R16/R17) |
| `includes` / `builds` | the anchored `.c` / build file | the included header / listed file |
`NEIGHBOR`: symbols defined just before/after `$OLD` in REQ-A (R1 ranges) found by name in `$ROOT`; the unknown
symbol between them is a candidate.

**L2 – fuzzy line grep** (signal `FUZZY`): R16 on the distinctive `+`/body lines of `$OLD` (skip `WEAK` patterns);
group the hits by enclosing block (R1 on each hit file). A block holding ≥2 non-WEAK hits is a candidate.

**L3 – stable anchors** (signal `ANCHOR`): from `$OLD`'s body take string literals, numeric constants other than
0/1/-1, data IDs (`STR_*`, NVRAM keys, command keywords) and `uses-external` callees; `grep -rnF` each (R13 for
data, all file types); count hits per enclosing block. A block holding ≥2 of them, and more than any other block,
is a candidate. Encoding: see L7.

**L4 – rename-invariant similarity** (signals `SIM`, `SIG`): R17. `SIM` when `blind` ≥ 0.6 and the result is not
`TOO-SHORT`; `SIG` when `sig` is `=`. `possible SPLIT` / `size` ≥ 2 → check `SPLIT_SYMBOL` / `MERGED_SYMBOL`.

**L5 – rename pattern** (signal `PATTERN`): when ≥2 symbols of this request are already anchored as renames with
the same textual rule (prefix/suffix/word change, e.g. `TonerSave_` → `Eco_`, `toner_save` → `eco_mode`), apply the
rule to `$OLD` and grep the predicted name (R2). Record the rule in `_work/alias_map.md` (`kind = pattern`).

**L6 – hypotheses** (signal `LLM`): synonyms, abbreviations, other naming conventions, the request's comments
(also non-English) → grep each guess (R2), then read the candidates and compare behavior with B1's
before → after sentence. A guess is only a lead: it never counts as evidence without a signal from L0–L4.

**L7 – nothing found: eliminate before concluding** (record which checks were done)
- macro-generated: `grep "${GOPT[@]}" -E '##|DEFINE_[A-Z_]*\(' "$ROOT"` near the anchored neighbors; parts of `$OLD` as macro args.
- encoding: for non-UTF-8 trees grep literals as bytes:
  `LC_ALL=C grep -a -rnF "$(printf '%s' "$LIT" | iconv -f UTF-8 -t SHIFT_JIS)" "$ROOT"` (use the encoding from `file -I`).
  `-a` is required: without it grep (and the `grep` wrapper of some agent shells) treats non-UTF-8 files as binary
  and silently skips them. Same for any grep of non-ASCII literals in non-UTF-8 trees (L3, R13).
- split / merged: R17 `possible SPLIT`, `size`.
- rewritten: stable anchors / data IDs of `$OLD` still present (L3) but no FUZZY/SIM match → `REWRITTEN`.
- removed: no anchor, no content match, and the linked ends no longer reference anything at that spot → `NOT_FOUND`
  with reason `removed` (B then sets latest state `REMOVED_IN_LATEST`).

**Signals → confidence** (no history exists; combine independent signals). Families: *relation* = `ALIAS`,
`EDGE`, `NEIGHBOR`; *content* = `FUZZY`, `ANCHOR`, `SIM`; *shape* = `SIG`; *naming* = `PATTERN`, `LLM`.
- `High`: `ALIAS`; or ≥1 relation + ≥1 content signal; or ≥3 agreeing signals from ≥2 families.
- `Medium`: 2 agreeing signals from 2 different families, not both naming (e.g. `SIM` + `SIG`, `FUZZY` + `PATTERN`).
- `Low`: a single signal, naming signals only, `SIM` below 0.6, or `TOO-SHORT` bodies with content signals only → ask.
- Downgrade one level when a link contradicts the candidate (cross-check fails, B2.3) or when two candidates are
  within 0.1 `blind` of each other with no other signal separating them.
Always list the signals in the evidence cell, e.g. `EDGE(N004 calls, SRC:src/print/render.c:88) + SIM 0.96 + SIG =`.
Old body spread over 2+ blocks → `SPLIT_SYMBOL`; 2+ old bodies inside one block → `MERGED_SYMBOL`.

## R13 – Data dependencies (search ALL file types, not only code)
```bash
grep -rnI -w --exclude-dir=.git "$TOKEN" "$ROOT"          # every text file: .c/.h, .csv, .xml, .json, .txt, .rc, .mk, linker scripts…
```
Checklist per kind:
- **String/message ID** (`STR_*`, `MSG_*`, resource IDs): the ID definition + the entry in **every** language/resource table.
- **Enum entry**: every array sized/indexed by the enum (`[X_COUNT]`, `[X_MAX]`), switch statements over it, tables in enum order.
- **Settings / NVRAM field**: struct field, default-value table, init/reset/factory-default function, version or
  layout number, checksum/CRC range, migration code, any range/limit table.
- **Registry entry**: menu/command/event/handler tables, dispatcher `case`, init sequence lists.
- **Config**: feature macros in config headers, Makefile/CMake defines, source lists, linker sections.
- **Data files**: tables, calibration/curve data, resource files referenced by name or by ID.

## R14 – Is a later change block related to the feature? (EXTENSION vs UNRELATED)
For a block of lines changed in latest source after the request (from `diff REQ-A-body latest-body`):
related signals –
1. the block's lines contain feature tokens (S names, feature macros, string IDs, `B_new_tokens.txt` project tokens);
2. the block is inside the feature's guard (R5);
3. the block edits or is within ±3 lines of the request's `+` lines;
4. comments in or next to the block naming the feature, the request or a request/ticket ID (R10 pattern).
≥1 of signals 1–3 (and none contradicting) → `EXTENSION` (new behavior) / `BUGFIX` (fixes feature lines) /
`REFACTOR` (renames/moves feature lines). None of them, and the block carries another feature's tokens/guard →
`UNRELATED`. Mixed or no signal → `UNCLEAR` (ask).

## R15 – Request link graph (Checkpoint A7)
Inputs: `_work/A_hunks.md` (owners), `_work/A_ranges/**` (R1 ranges), REQ-A (REQ-B for deleted items).
`$RA` = `$SOURCE_REQUEST/After`. Work only inside the request; endpoints outside it become `external` nodes.
```bash
# node names: owners of modification points + data items added on + lines
awk -F'|' 'NR>2{print $8}' "$W/A_hunks.md" | sed 's/ (.*//;s/^ *//;s/@.*//' | grep -v '^Not identified$' | sort -u > "$W/A_node_names.txt"  # 'symbol (kind)' column
#   then append the data items added on + lines (string IDs, enum entries, fields, macros) found while reading the hunks
# calls / reads / writes / registers / localizes / defaults / indexes: every use of a node name inside another node's range
while read -r n; do grep "${GOPT[@]}" -nw -- "$n" "$RA"; done < "$W/A_node_names.txt" > "$W/A_uses.txt"
#   for each hit: the enclosing range (A_ranges, R1) is the 'from' node; decide the type from the line:
#   'n(' → calls · inside an initializer table → registers · inside an enum-sized array / switch(case n) → indexes ·
#   in a language/resource table → localizes · in a default/init/reset function → defaults · 'x->n =' / 'n =' → writes · else reads
# declares: prototypes / externs of node names in headers
grep -rn --include='*.h' -E "^[^#].*[^A-Za-z0-9_](NAME)[[:space:]]*\(" "$RA"      # NAME = node name; one per node
# includes: request headers included by request files
grep -rn -E '^[[:space:]]*#[[:space:]]*include' "$RA" | grep -F -f <(find "$RA" -name '*.h' -exec basename {} \;)
# builds: request source files listed in build files
find "$RA" -type f \( -name Makefile -o -name '*.mk' -o -name CMakeLists.txt -o -name '*.cmake' \) -exec \
  grep -nF -f <(find "$RA" -name '*.c' -o -name '*.cpp' | xargs -n1 basename) {} +
# guards: R5 on each + line; nodes inside the same #if/#ifdef share a 'guards' edge with the macro node
# uses-external: R4 tokens of the node's + lines that are not node names and not standard/library
```
Each edge row: `from | type | to | REQ-A:path:line`. Stability classes are in `checkpoints/A-diff.md` A7.

## R16 – Fuzzy line grep (rename-tolerant)
Turns one source line into a POSIX ERE where only the identifiers that may have been renamed become wildcards;
literals, keywords, operators and unchanged names stay literal. Works with BSD and GNU grep.
```bash
P=$(python3 -I "$SK/scripts/fuzzy_line.py" --abstract-file "$W/B_feature_ids.txt" "$LINE")   # stderr: kept=… wild=… [WEAK]
grep "${GOPT[@]}" -nE -e "$P" "$ROOT"
```
- `B_feature_ids.txt` = names defined by the request (nodes of `A_links.md` with stability `medium`/`volatile`),
  one per line. Without `--abstract-file` every non-keyword identifier becomes a wildcard (weaker).
- Use only distinctive lines; a `WEAK` pattern (fewer than 3 literal tokens, e.g. `i = 0;`) is never a signal alone.
- One-line patterns miss statements split over several lines and reformatted logic: R17 covers those.
- No `python3`: build the pattern by hand – replace each feature identifier by `[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*`, escape
  `. [ ] ( ) * + ? { } | ^ $ \` as `[.]`…, and put `[[:space:]]*` between tokens.

## R17 – Rename-invariant similarity (whole body)
Compares one REQ-A block (function, table, struct/enum) with **every** top-level block of `$ROOT`. Deterministic,
standard-library Python, no embeddings. Comments and whitespace are ignored; every non-keyword identifier becomes
`$I` (so renames do not matter) while literals, keywords and operators are kept; 4-token shingles are compared by
containment (= share of the reference that is still present, so a function that grew after the request is not penalised).
```bash
python3 -I "$SK/scripts/similarity.py" --ref-file "$SOURCE_REQUEST/After/$P" --ref-name "$OLD" \
        --root "$ROOT" --feature-ids "$W/B_feature_ids.txt" --top 5          # or --ref-lines a-b ; --json
```
Columns: `blind` (containment, rename-proof), `named` (only feature ids abstracted; stricter), `size` (candidate /
reference tokens), `lits` (shared literals), `calls` (shared callee names), `sig` (`=` same parameter count and
return/storage tokens, `~` same count, `!` different). `TOO-SHORT` (< 15 tokens) → scores unreliable, not a `SIM` signal.
`possible SPLIT` → two blocks together cover ≥ 60 % of the reference.
Reading: `blind` ≥ 0.8 strong, 0.6–0.8 candidate, < 0.6 not the same block. `size` ≥ 2 with high `blind` → the block
grew a lot (EXTENSION) or absorbed other code (MERGED): read it. Limits: complete rewrites (no shared structure) and
heavy macro code are not detected; preprocessor lines are ignored.
No `python3` → skip R16/R17 and record `SIM/FUZZY not available (python3 missing)` in the evidence.
# Decision table (Checkpoint D port classes)

Inputs: B (anchoring, evolution, extensions, closure) and C (target state). Apply top to bottom; the first
matching row wins. `Interactive` = what to do in `interactive` mode; `Auto default` = `APPROVAL_MODE=auto`
behaviour (mark `AUTO-DECIDED`). **Content source by default = the port version from latest source (B5).**

| # | Condition | Port class | Action | Interactive | Auto default |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Anchor `NOT_FOUND` / `REWRITTEN` / `MACRO_GENERATED` / `REMOVED_IN_LATEST` / hunk `GONE` in latest source | `SOURCE_GONE` | Do not port blindly; maybe the feature was reverted or rewritten | **ask, stop** | port REQ-A version, HIGH risk flag |
| 2 | Any `Low` confidence or `RENAMED_CANDIDATE` (source or target) | `NEEDS_CONFIRMATION` | No code planned until confirmed | **ask, stop** | `Blocked` for that M |
| 3 | Change type `cosmetic` only | `SKIP_COSMETIC` | Port only if the symbol is ported anyway | plan | plan |
| 4 | Target state `SAME_AS_SOURCE` (incl. equal modulo aliases) | `SKIP_ALREADY_PRESENT` | No change; cite evidence | plan | plan |
| 5 | Evolution has `UNRELATED` blocks in a ported symbol | `TAKE_LATEST_PARTIAL` | Port request + extension/bugfix/refactor lines only; list excluded lines | **ask** | partial take, flag |
| 6 | Target state `SAME_AS_BEFORE` | `APPLY_PORT_VERSION` | Replace the symbol body with the port version (or 3-way merge, see E) | plan | plan |
| 7 | Target `MISSING`, item is a request symbol or `ext` | `COPY_NEW` | Copy the port version; add declaration/header entries as in source | plan (list `ext` items as *scope beyond request*) | plan, flag `ext` |
| 8 | Target `MISSING`, item is a code dependency | `COPY_DEPENDENCY` | Copy latest definition from `SOURCE_ROOT` | plan | plan |
| 9 | Target `MISSING`, item is a data dependency (string, table entry, default, resource, enum entry) | `ADD_DATA` | Add the entry in **every** required place (all languages, all tables sized by the enum, defaults, version/checksum) in target style | plan | plan |
| 10 | Ported code references a symbol the target has under another confirmed name (`RENAMED`/`MOVED`) | `ALIAS_ADAPT` | Rewrite only those identifiers/includes in the ported text per alias map; list each substitution | plan | plan, flag |
| 11 | Guard macro of a ported line not enabled in target | `ENABLE_GUARD` | Add the define where the target enables sibling features (cite it) | **ask**: enable in target? | add, flag |
| 12 | Target `DIVERGED` | `ADAPT_MERGE` | 3-way merge: base REQ-B, ours target, theirs port version; keep target-only lines | ask on any conflict | merge; conflict → `Blocked` for that P |
| 13 | `SIGNATURE_DIFF` and target symbol has target callers | `CONFLICT` | Options: (a) keep target symbol, adapt ported call sites; (b) change target symbol + all target callers; (c) add new symbol | **ask, stop** | (a), flag |
| 14 | `SIGNATURE_DIFF`, no target callers | `REPLACE` | Replace with port version | plan | plan |
| 15 | Change type `layout` on persistent/shared data (NVRAM, protocol, file format, enum values used as IDs) | `LAYOUT_RISK` | Port as in source; record offset/value shift as HIGH risk | **ask** | port + HIGH risk |
| 16 | Item is a `CONSUMER` (another source feature uses this one) | `REPORT_ONLY` | Never copy; list | plan | plan |
| 17 | Incoming registration needed for behavior and missing in target | `ADD_REGISTRATION` | Add the single entry/call the feature needs, in target table style | plan | plan |
| 18 | Non-code file (build, resource) needed for build/behavior | `NON_CODE` | Port the needed entry (e.g. add new .c to Makefile); otherwise report | plan | plan |
| 19 | Nothing above matches | `UNCLASSIFIED` | Do not guess | **ask** | `Blocked` |

Rules:
- Every P-id states its content source: `SRC:<path>:<lines>` (port version) or `REQ-A:<path>:<lines>` (only when row 1 chose it).
- An item may need several classes (e.g. `COPY_NEW` + `ALIAS_ADAPT`): create one M per class, all naming the same item.
- New source files must be added to the target build (R9) as their own P-id.
- "Adaptation" column: `none` for verbatim copy; otherwise the exact difference from the source text and why (alias, partial take, conflict option).
