# Search recipes (C/C++ and similar)

Copy-paste commands. `$ROOT` = the root searched, `$S` = symbol name, `$F` = file, `$W` = `$OUTPUT_ROOT/_work`,
`$SK` = this skill's directory (scripts in `$SK/scripts/`, run with `python3 -I`).
Common grep options (define once per shell):
```bash
GOPT=(-rn --include='*.c' --include='*.h' --include='*.cc' --include='*.cpp' --include='*.cxx' \
      --include='*.hpp' --include='*.hh' --include='*.inc' --exclude-dir=.git --exclude-dir=build --exclude-dir=out)
```
macOS grep: `-w` is reliable; if `\b` misbehaves inside `-E`, use `-w` or `[[:<:]]` / `[[:>:]]`.
Always read results narrowly: `sed -n '<a>,<b>p' "$F"`.

## R0 – Diff of the request
```bash
cd "$SOURCE_REQUEST"
diff -rq Before After                                   # file list (Only in / differ)
git diff --no-index --no-color -U3 --function-context -- "Before/$P" "After/$P" > "$OUTPUT_ROOT/diffs/source/$P.diff"
git diff --no-index --no-color -U0 -- "Before/$P" "After/$P"     # exact changed line numbers
git diff --no-index --stat Before After                  # sanity count
```
For an added file use `/dev/null` as the Before side; for a deleted file `/dev/null` as After.
`git diff --no-index` works on plain folders (no repository needed) and exits 1 when files differ: not an error.
Binary: `git diff --no-index --numstat` shows `-  -` → `file_status` stays as computed, function `N/A (non-code file)`.

Fallback without `git` (same information, standard `diff`):
```bash
diff -u -p "Before/$P" "After/$P" > "$OUTPUT_ROOT/diffs/source/$P.diff"    # -N for added/deleted: diff -u -p -N
diff -U0 "Before/$P" "After/$P"                                            # exact changed line numbers
diff -ruN Before After | grep -E '^\+' | grep -vc '^+++ '                 # added lines total
diff -ruN Before After | grep -E '^-'  | grep -vc '^--- '                  # deleted lines total
```

## R1 – Top-level symbol ranges of a file (function / struct / enum / table bodies)
```bash
awk '
function trim(s){gsub(/^[ \t]+|[ \t]+$/,"",s);return s}
{ raw=$0; code=raw; sub(/\/\/.*/,"",code)
  o=gsub(/\{/,"{",code); c=gsub(/\}/,"}",code)
  if (depth==0 && o>0) { if (trim(code)!="{") {hdr=raw; hs=NR} else {hdr=prev; hs=prevNR} }
  depth+=o-c
  if (depth==0 && o+c>0 && hs) { printf "%d-%d\t%s\n", hs, NR, trim(hdr); hs=0 }
  if (depth==0 && trim(code)!="") { prev=raw; prevNR=NR } }' "$F"
```
Output `start-end<TAB>header`. A changed line inside a range belongs to that symbol.
Limitations – verify by reading the header lines when: the signature spans several lines (header
shows only the last line), braces appear in strings/`/* */` comments, or code sits in `#if 0`.
Lines outside every range: classify with R2 (`#define`, prototype, global, `#include` → file scope).

## R2 – Definitions
```bash
grep "${GOPT[@]}" -E "^[A-Za-z_][^;]*[^A-Za-z0-9_]$S[[:space:]]*\(" "$ROOT" | grep -v ';[[:space:]]*$'   # function definition
grep "${GOPT[@]}" -E "[^A-Za-z0-9_]$S[[:space:]]*\([^)]*\)?[[:space:]]*;" "$ROOT" | grep -v '=' # prototype
grep "${GOPT[@]}" -E "^[[:space:]]*#[[:space:]]*define[[:space:]]+$S([^A-Za-z0-9_]|$)" "$ROOT"     # macro
grep "${GOPT[@]}" -E "(struct|union|enum)[[:space:]]+$S([^A-Za-z0-9_]|$)" "$ROOT"                  # tag
grep "${GOPT[@]}" -E "^\}[[:space:]]*$S[[:space:]]*;|typedef[^;]*[^A-Za-z0-9_]$S[[:space:]]*;" "$ROOT"  # typedef
grep "${GOPT[@]}" -wE "$S[[:space:]]*(=[^=]|,|$)" "$ROOT"                                          # enum constant (check it is inside an enum)
grep "${GOPT[@]}" -E "^[A-Za-z_][^(]*[^A-Za-z0-9_]$S[[:space:]]*(\[[^]]*\])?[[:space:]]*(=|;)" "$ROOT"   # global / table
```
Static symbols may be defined in several files: always record the file and use `name@path`.

## R3 – Uses
```bash
grep "${GOPT[@]}" -w "$S" "$ROOT"                                  # every use
grep "${GOPT[@]}" -E "(^|[^A-Za-z0-9_])$S[[:space:]]*\(" "$ROOT"   # calls
grep "${GOPT[@]}" -w "$S" "$ROOT" | grep -vE "$S[[:space:]]*\("    # non-call uses: function pointers, registration tables, callbacks
```
Registration tables (menus, command tables, handler arrays, init lists) are the most common hidden
incoming dependency: for every non-call use, read the enclosing table (R1) and note the entry.

## R4 – New tokens introduced by the request (outgoing dependencies)
```bash
grep -h '^+' "$OUTPUT_ROOT"/diffs/source/*.diff | grep -v '^+++' \
 | sed -e 's://.*$::' -e 's:"[^"]*"::g' | grep -oE '[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*' | sort -u > "$OUTPUT_ROOT/_work/B_new_tokens.txt"
```
Remove C/C++ keywords and standard types/library names (`if for while return sizeof static const
unsigned int char void struct enum union typedef extern inline bool true false NULL uint8_t … memcpy printf …`).
**Follow only these tokens** (tokens the request adds). Do not walk whole shared tables or files that
the request merely touches – only the hunks are ported.

## R5 – Enclosing preprocessor conditions of line N
```bash
awk -v N="$N" '
/^[ \t]*#[ \t]*(if|ifdef|ifndef)/ { st[++d]=$0 }
/^[ \t]*#[ \t]*(elif|else)/        { st[d]=st[d]" / "$0 }
/^[ \t]*#[ \t]*endif/              { d-- }
NR==N { for(i=1;i<=d;i++) print st[i]; exit }' "$F"
```
For each macro `M` in the condition, check where it is enabled:
```bash
grep "${GOPT[@]}" --include='Makefile' --include='*.mk' --include='CMakeLists.txt' --include='*.cmake' \
     -E "#[[:space:]]*define[[:space:]]+$M([^A-Za-z0-9_]|$)|-D$M([^A-Za-z0-9_]|$)|$M[[:space:]]*[:+]?=" "$ROOT"
```

## R6 – Headers / includes
```bash
grep "${GOPT[@]}" -E '#[[:space:]]*include' "$F"                    # what a file includes
grep "${GOPT[@]}" -E "#[[:space:]]*include[[:space:]]*[<\"]([^>\"]*/)?$(basename "$H")[>\"]" "$ROOT"   # who includes header H
```

## R7 – Compare one symbol across trees
```bash
sed -n '<a>,<b>p' "$FILE_1" > "$OUTPUT_ROOT/_work/cmp_1.txt"
sed -n '<c>,<d>p' "$FILE_2" > "$OUTPUT_ROOT/_work/cmp_2.txt"
diff -w "$OUTPUT_ROOT/_work/cmp_1.txt" "$OUTPUT_ROOT/_work/cmp_2.txt" && echo SAME
```
Get the ranges with R1 on each file. Compare target vs `REQ-B` and target vs `REQ-A` to decide the
target state; compare `SRC` vs `REQ-A` for drift.

## R8 – Rename candidates (only when the name is MISSING in target)
Take 1–2 distinctive lines of the source body (string literals, unusual constants, unique call
sequences) and search for them in the target:
```bash
grep "${GOPT[@]}" -F '<distinctive literal>' "$TARGET_ROOT"
```
A hit is a `RENAMED_CANDIDATE` with confidence `Low` until the user confirms.

## R9 – Tests and build entry points
```bash
find "$ROOT" -type d \( -iname 'test*' -o -iname 'unittest*' -o -iname 'ut' \) -not -path '*/.git/*'
grep "${GOPT[@]}" -lw "$S" "$ROOT" | grep -iE 'test|_ut|spec'
ls "$ROOT" | grep -iE '^(Makefile|GNUmakefile|CMakeLists.txt|build.*\.(sh|bat|py)|.*\.sln|.*\.vcxproj|README.*)$'
```

## R10 – Request-label convention in target
```bash
grep "${GOPT[@]}" -E '(REQ|CR|PR|ECR|ECO|TICKET|ISSUE|BUG|FIX|MOD|CHG)[-_#: ]?[0-9]{2,}' "$TARGET_ROOT" | head -50
```
Accept a convention only if ≥3 occurrences share one format (prefix, comment style, start/end
markers). Record 3 examples as evidence.

## R11 – Relocate a file (moved / renamed / split)
`$P` = request-relative path, `$REF` = the reference file (REQ-A version for source anchoring, the source
version for target lookup), `$W` = `$OUTPUT_ROOT/_work`.
```bash
# a. same basename elsewhere
find "$ROOT" -type f -name "$(basename "$P")" -not -path '*/.git/*'
# b. includes: who includes the old header name / a header with the same symbols (R6) – a moved header is
#    usually still included by the same .c files under a new path
# c. content similarity: rank candidate files by shared normalized lines
norm(){ sed -e 's://.*$::' -e 's/^[[:space:]]*//' -e 's/[[:space:]]*$//' "$1" | grep -vE '^([{}();]*|/\*.*|\*.*)$' | sort -u; }
norm "$REF" > "$W/ref.lines"; total=$(wc -l < "$W/ref.lines")
grep -oE '[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]{6,}' "$REF" | sort | uniq -c | sort -n | head -15 | awk '{print $2}' > "$W/ref.ids"
grep "${GOPT[@]}" -lwF -f "$W/ref.ids" "$ROOT" | sed 's/:.*//' | sort -u | while read -r c; do
  n=$(norm "$c" | comm -12 - "$W/ref.lines" | wc -l); echo "$((100*n/total))% $c"; done | sort -rn | head -5
```
Relation signals for files (from `_work/A_links.md`): an anchored `.c` still `includes` a header at the same
place, or an anchored build file `builds` the candidate. File confidence follows the R12 rules with these as
relation signals and the similarity score as content signal.
Score ≥ 60 % → strong candidate; 30–60 % → candidate (maybe `SPLIT_FILE`: check whether 2 candidates together
cover the file); < 30 % → not the same file. The `ref.ids` are the *rarest* long identifiers of the file.
d. When the file's identifiers were renamed too (a–c find nothing): run R17 for the 2–3 largest blocks of `$REF`;
   the file that holds their top candidates is the file candidate (blocks landing in 2+ files → maybe `SPLIT_FILE`).

## R12 – Locate a symbol whose name is not found (search ladder)
`$OLD` = request name, body from REQ-A (from latest source when used for the target lookup in C).
`$W` = `$OUTPUT_ROOT/_work`, `$SK` = this skill's directory. Run the rungs **in order**; stop climbing as soon as
the confidence rules below give `High`, otherwise collect every candidate and its signals.
A missing name alone proves nothing: it may be a rename, a macro-generated name, a split/merge, a rewrite,
a removal or an encoding mismatch (L7 tells them apart).

**L0 – alias / wrapper** (signal `ALIAS`)
```bash
grep "${GOPT[@]}" -E "#[[:space:]]*define[[:space:]]+$OLD[[:space:](]" "$ROOT"
grep "${GOPT[@]}" -B2 -A6 -E "^[A-Za-z_].*[^A-Za-z0-9_]$OLD[[:space:]]*\(" "$ROOT" | grep -E 'return .*\('   # thin wrapper
grep "${GOPT[@]}" -w "$OLD" "$ROOT"     # also catches the old name left in comments ("renamed from …")
```
**L1 – walk the links** (signals `EDGE`, `NEIGHBOR`). For every edge of `$OLD` in `_work/A_links.md` whose other
end is already anchored in `$ROOT`, read that end's latest body and find the spot that played the edge's role:
| edge | where to look in the anchored end | the candidate is |
|---|---|---|
| `calls` (anchored caller → `$OLD`) | the caller's latest body; find the request call line with R16 | the function called at that position |
| `calls` (`$OLD` → anchored callee) | callers of the callee (R3) whose body matches `$OLD` (R16/R17) | that caller |
| `declares` | the header next to the anchored prototypes (same order) | the prototype in that slot |
| `registers` | the anchored table; entry with the same ID/key/slot | the handler/ID in that entry |
| `indexes` / `localizes` / `defaults` | the anchored enum, language table or default table; same position/value | the entry there |
| `reads` / `writes` | functions using the anchored field/global (R3) | the one whose body matches (R16/R17) |
| `includes` / `builds` | the anchored `.c` / build file | the included header / listed file |
`NEIGHBOR`: symbols defined just before/after `$OLD` in REQ-A (R1 ranges) found by name in `$ROOT`; the unknown
symbol between them is a candidate.

**L2 – fuzzy line grep** (signal `FUZZY`): R16 on the distinctive `+`/body lines of `$OLD` (skip `WEAK` patterns);
group the hits by enclosing block (R1 on each hit file). A block holding ≥2 non-WEAK hits is a candidate.

**L3 – stable anchors** (signal `ANCHOR`): from `$OLD`'s body take string literals, numeric constants other than
0/1/-1, data IDs (`STR_*`, NVRAM keys, command keywords) and `uses-external` callees; `grep -rnF` each (R13 for
data, all file types); count hits per enclosing block. A block holding ≥2 of them, and more than any other block,
is a candidate. Encoding: see L7.

**L4 – rename-invariant similarity** (signals `SIM`, `SIG`): R17. `SIM` when `blind` ≥ 0.6 and the result is not
`TOO-SHORT`; `SIG` when `sig` is `=`. `possible SPLIT` / `size` ≥ 2 → check `SPLIT_SYMBOL` / `MERGED_SYMBOL`.

**L5 – rename pattern** (signal `PATTERN`): when ≥2 symbols of this request are already anchored as renames with
the same textual rule (prefix/suffix/word change, e.g. `TonerSave_` → `Eco_`, `toner_save` → `eco_mode`), apply the
rule to `$OLD` and grep the predicted name (R2). Record the rule in `_work/alias_map.md` (`kind = pattern`).

**L6 – hypotheses** (signal `LLM`): synonyms, abbreviations, other naming conventions, the request's comments
(also non-English) → grep each guess (R2), then read the candidates and compare behavior with B1's
before → after sentence. A guess is only a lead: it never counts as evidence without a signal from L0–L4.

**L7 – nothing found: eliminate before concluding** (record which checks were done)
- macro-generated: `grep "${GOPT[@]}" -E '##|DEFINE_[A-Z_]*\(' "$ROOT"` near the anchored neighbors; parts of `$OLD` as macro args.
- encoding: for non-UTF-8 trees grep literals as bytes:
  `LC_ALL=C grep -a -rnF "$(printf '%s' "$LIT" | iconv -f UTF-8 -t SHIFT_JIS)" "$ROOT"` (use the encoding from `file -I`).
  `-a` is required: without it grep (and the `grep` wrapper of some agent shells) treats non-UTF-8 files as binary
  and silently skips them. Same for any grep of non-ASCII literals in non-UTF-8 trees (L3, R13).
- split / merged: R17 `possible SPLIT`, `size`.
- rewritten: stable anchors / data IDs of `$OLD` still present (L3) but no FUZZY/SIM match → `REWRITTEN`.
- removed: no anchor, no content match, and the linked ends no longer reference anything at that spot → `NOT_FOUND`
  with reason `removed` (B then sets latest state `REMOVED_IN_LATEST`).

**Signals → confidence** (no history exists; combine independent signals). Families: *relation* = `ALIAS`,
`EDGE`, `NEIGHBOR`; *content* = `FUZZY`, `ANCHOR`, `SIM`; *shape* = `SIG`; *naming* = `PATTERN`, `LLM`.
- `High`: `ALIAS`; or ≥1 relation + ≥1 content signal; or ≥3 agreeing signals from ≥2 families.
- `Medium`: 2 agreeing signals from 2 different families, not both naming (e.g. `SIM` + `SIG`, `FUZZY` + `PATTERN`).
- `Low`: a single signal, naming signals only, `SIM` below 0.6, or `TOO-SHORT` bodies with content signals only → ask.
- Downgrade one level when a link contradicts the candidate (cross-check fails, B2.3) or when two candidates are
  within 0.1 `blind` of each other with no other signal separating them.
Always list the signals in the evidence cell, e.g. `EDGE(N004 calls, SRC:src/print/render.c:88) + SIM 0.96 + SIG =`.
Old body spread over 2+ blocks → `SPLIT_SYMBOL`; 2+ old bodies inside one block → `MERGED_SYMBOL`.

## R13 – Data dependencies (search ALL file types, not only code)
```bash
grep -rnI -w --exclude-dir=.git "$TOKEN" "$ROOT"          # every text file: .c/.h, .csv, .xml, .json, .txt, .rc, .mk, linker scripts…
```
Checklist per kind:
- **String/message ID** (`STR_*`, `MSG_*`, resource IDs): the ID definition + the entry in **every** language/resource table.
- **Enum entry**: every array sized/indexed by the enum (`[X_COUNT]`, `[X_MAX]`), switch statements over it, tables in enum order.
- **Settings / NVRAM field**: struct field, default-value table, init/reset/factory-default function, version or
  layout number, checksum/CRC range, migration code, any range/limit table.
- **Registry entry**: menu/command/event/handler tables, dispatcher `case`, init sequence lists.
- **Config**: feature macros in config headers, Makefile/CMake defines, source lists, linker sections.
- **Data files**: tables, calibration/curve data, resource files referenced by name or by ID.

## R14 – Is a later change block related to the feature? (EXTENSION vs UNRELATED)
For a block of lines changed in latest source after the request (from `diff REQ-A-body latest-body`):
related signals –
1. the block's lines contain feature tokens (S names, feature macros, string IDs, `B_new_tokens.txt` project tokens);
2. the block is inside the feature's guard (R5);
3. the block edits or is within ±3 lines of the request's `+` lines;
4. comments in or next to the block naming the feature, the request or a request/ticket ID (R10 pattern).
≥1 of signals 1–3 (and none contradicting) → `EXTENSION` (new behavior) / `BUGFIX` (fixes feature lines) /
`REFACTOR` (renames/moves feature lines). None of them, and the block carries another feature's tokens/guard →
`UNRELATED`. Mixed or no signal → `UNCLEAR` (ask).

## R15 – Request link graph (Checkpoint A7)
Inputs: `_work/A_hunks.md` (owners), `_work/A_ranges/**` (R1 ranges), REQ-A (REQ-B for deleted items).
`$RA` = `$SOURCE_REQUEST/After`. Work only inside the request; endpoints outside it become `external` nodes.
```bash
# node names: owners of modification points + data items added on + lines
awk -F'|' 'NR>2{print $8}' "$W/A_hunks.md" | sed 's/ (.*//;s/^ *//;s/@.*//' | grep -v '^Not identified$' | sort -u > "$W/A_node_names.txt"  # 'symbol (kind)' column
#   then append the data items added on + lines (string IDs, enum entries, fields, macros) found while reading the hunks
# calls / reads / writes / registers / localizes / defaults / indexes: every use of a node name inside another node's range
while read -r n; do grep "${GOPT[@]}" -nw -- "$n" "$RA"; done < "$W/A_node_names.txt" > "$W/A_uses.txt"
#   for each hit: the enclosing range (A_ranges, R1) is the 'from' node; decide the type from the line:
#   'n(' → calls · inside an initializer table → registers · inside an enum-sized array / switch(case n) → indexes ·
#   in a language/resource table → localizes · in a default/init/reset function → defaults · 'x->n =' / 'n =' → writes · else reads
# declares: prototypes / externs of node names in headers
grep -rn --include='*.h' -E "^[^#].*[^A-Za-z0-9_](NAME)[[:space:]]*\(" "$RA"      # NAME = node name; one per node
# includes: request headers included by request files
grep -rn -E '^[[:space:]]*#[[:space:]]*include' "$RA" | grep -F -f <(find "$RA" -name '*.h' -exec basename {} \;)
# builds: request source files listed in build files
find "$RA" -type f \( -name Makefile -o -name '*.mk' -o -name CMakeLists.txt -o -name '*.cmake' \) -exec \
  grep -nF -f <(find "$RA" -name '*.c' -o -name '*.cpp' | xargs -n1 basename) {} +
# guards: R5 on each + line; nodes inside the same #if/#ifdef share a 'guards' edge with the macro node
# uses-external: R4 tokens of the node's + lines that are not node names and not standard/library
```
Each edge row: `from | type | to | REQ-A:path:line`. Stability classes are in `checkpoints/A-diff.md` A7.

## R16 – Fuzzy line grep (rename-tolerant)
Turns one source line into a POSIX ERE where only the identifiers that may have been renamed become wildcards;
literals, keywords, operators and unchanged names stay literal. Works with BSD and GNU grep.
```bash
P=$(python3 -I "$SK/scripts/fuzzy_line.py" --abstract-file "$W/B_feature_ids.txt" "$LINE")   # stderr: kept=… wild=… [WEAK]
grep "${GOPT[@]}" -nE -e "$P" "$ROOT"
```
- `B_feature_ids.txt` = names defined by the request (nodes of `A_links.md` with stability `medium`/`volatile`),
  one per line. Without `--abstract-file` every non-keyword identifier becomes a wildcard (weaker).
- Use only distinctive lines; a `WEAK` pattern (fewer than 3 literal tokens, e.g. `i = 0;`) is never a signal alone.
- One-line patterns miss statements split over several lines and reformatted logic: R17 covers those.
- No `python3`: build the pattern by hand – replace each feature identifier by `[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*`, escape
  `. [ ] ( ) * + ? { } | ^ $ \` as `[.]`…, and put `[[:space:]]*` between tokens.

## R17 – Rename-invariant similarity (whole body)
Compares one REQ-A block (function, table, struct/enum) with **every** top-level block of `$ROOT`. Deterministic,
standard-library Python, no embeddings. Comments and whitespace are ignored; every non-keyword identifier becomes
`$I` (so renames do not matter) while literals, keywords and operators are kept; 4-token shingles are compared by
containment (= share of the reference that is still present, so a function that grew after the request is not penalised).
```bash
python3 -I "$SK/scripts/similarity.py" --ref-file "$SOURCE_REQUEST/After/$P" --ref-name "$OLD" \
        --root "$ROOT" --feature-ids "$W/B_feature_ids.txt" --top 5          # or --ref-lines a-b ; --json
```
Columns: `blind` (containment, rename-proof), `named` (only feature ids abstracted; stricter), `size` (candidate /
reference tokens), `lits` (shared literals), `calls` (shared callee names), `sig` (`=` same parameter count and
return/storage tokens, `~` same count, `!` different). `TOO-SHORT` (< 15 tokens) → scores unreliable, not a `SIM` signal.
`possible SPLIT` → two blocks together cover ≥ 60 % of the reference.
Reading: `blind` ≥ 0.8 strong, 0.6–0.8 candidate, < 0.6 not the same block. `size` ≥ 2 with high `blind` → the block
grew a lot (EXTENSION) or absorbed other code (MERGED): read it. Limits: complete rewrites (no shared structure) and
heavy macro code are not detected; preprocessor lines are ignored.
No `python3` → skip R16/R17 and record `SIM/FUZZY not available (python3 missing)` in the evidence.
# Decision table (Checkpoint D port classes)

Inputs: B (anchoring, evolution, extensions, closure) and C (target state). Apply top to bottom; the first
matching row wins. `Interactive` = what to do in `interactive` mode; `Auto default` = `APPROVAL_MODE=auto`
behaviour (mark `AUTO-DECIDED`). **Content source by default = the port version from latest source (B5).**

| # | Condition | Port class | Action | Interactive | Auto default |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Anchor `NOT_FOUND` / `REWRITTEN` / `MACRO_GENERATED` / `REMOVED_IN_LATEST` / hunk `GONE` in latest source | `SOURCE_GONE` | Do not port blindly; maybe the feature was reverted or rewritten | **ask, stop** | port REQ-A version, HIGH risk flag |
| 2 | Any `Low` confidence or `RENAMED_CANDIDATE` (source or target) | `NEEDS_CONFIRMATION` | No code planned until confirmed | **ask, stop** | `Blocked` for that M |
| 3 | Change type `cosmetic` only | `SKIP_COSMETIC` | Port only if the symbol is ported anyway | plan | plan |
| 4 | Target state `SAME_AS_SOURCE` (incl. equal modulo aliases) | `SKIP_ALREADY_PRESENT` | No change; cite evidence | plan | plan |
| 5 | Evolution has `UNRELATED` blocks in a ported symbol | `TAKE_LATEST_PARTIAL` | Port request + extension/bugfix/refactor lines only; list excluded lines | **ask** | partial take, flag |
| 6 | Target state `SAME_AS_BEFORE` | `APPLY_PORT_VERSION` | Replace the symbol body with the port version (or 3-way merge, see E) | plan | plan |
| 7 | Target `MISSING`, item is a request symbol or `ext` | `COPY_NEW` | Copy the port version; add declaration/header entries as in source | plan (list `ext` items as *scope beyond request*) | plan, flag `ext` |
| 8 | Target `MISSING`, item is a code dependency | `COPY_DEPENDENCY` | Copy latest definition from `SOURCE_ROOT` | plan | plan |
| 9 | Target `MISSING`, item is a data dependency (string, table entry, default, resource, enum entry) | `ADD_DATA` | Add the entry in **every** required place (all languages, all tables sized by the enum, defaults, version/checksum) in target style | plan | plan |
| 10 | Ported code references a symbol the target has under another confirmed name (`RENAMED`/`MOVED`) | `ALIAS_ADAPT` | Rewrite only those identifiers/includes in the ported text per alias map; list each substitution | plan | plan, flag |
| 11 | Guard macro of a ported line not enabled in target | `ENABLE_GUARD` | Add the define where the target enables sibling features (cite it) | **ask**: enable in target? | add, flag |
| 12 | Target `DIVERGED` | `ADAPT_MERGE` | 3-way merge: base REQ-B, ours target, theirs port version; keep target-only lines | ask on any conflict | merge; conflict → `Blocked` for that P |
| 13 | `SIGNATURE_DIFF` and target symbol has target callers | `CONFLICT` | Options: (a) keep target symbol, adapt ported call sites; (b) change target symbol + all target callers; (c) add new symbol | **ask, stop** | (a), flag |
| 14 | `SIGNATURE_DIFF`, no target callers | `REPLACE` | Replace with port version | plan | plan |
| 15 | Change type `layout` on persistent/shared data (NVRAM, protocol, file format, enum values used as IDs) | `LAYOUT_RISK` | Port as in source; record offset/value shift as HIGH risk | **ask** | port + HIGH risk |
| 16 | Item is a `CONSUMER` (another source feature uses this one) | `REPORT_ONLY` | Never copy; list | plan | plan |
| 17 | Incoming registration needed for behavior and missing in target | `ADD_REGISTRATION` | Add the single entry/call the feature needs, in target table style | plan | plan |
| 18 | Non-code file (build, resource) needed for build/behavior | `NON_CODE` | Port the needed entry (e.g. add new .c to Makefile); otherwise report | plan | plan |
| 19 | Nothing above matches | `UNCLASSIFIED` | Do not guess | **ask** | `Blocked` |

Rules:
- Every P-id states its content source: `SRC:<path>:<lines>` (port version) or `REQ-A:<path>:<lines>` (only when row 1 chose it).
- An item may need several classes (e.g. `COPY_NEW` + `ALIAS_ADAPT`): create one M per class, all naming the same item.
- New source files must be added to the target build (R9) as their own P-id.
- "Adaptation" column: `none` for verbatim copy; otherwise the exact difference from the source text and why (alias, partial take, conflict option).

# Checkpoint B – Source Change Analysis (anchor in latest source + feature closure)

**Goal:** starting from the request diff, trace back into `SOURCE_ROOT` (latest source), find where
every piece of the request lives *now* (even if files or functions were moved or renamed), find how the
feature was **extended** after the request, and collect the full closure of code **and data** the feature
needs. The result is the *port version* of the feature: what will be merged to the target.
**Reads:** `_work/A_hunks.md`, `_work/A_links.md`, `diffs/source/**`, `SOURCE_REQUEST/Before|After`, `SOURCE_ROOT` (search and
narrow reads; plain folder, no history – everything is inferred from content).
**Writes:** `_work/B_feature_ids.txt`, `_work/B_aliased/**`, `_work/B_anchor.md`, `_work/alias_map.md`, `_work/B_new_tokens.txt`,
`_work/B_symbols.md`, report section B.
**Load:** `references/c-cpp-search-recipes.md` (R1–R7, R9, R11–R17), `references/glossary.md`; uses `_work/A_links.md`.

## Steps

### B1 – Changed symbols (request view)
From `_work/A_hunks.md` create one `S###` per distinct symbol (several H-ids may share one S). For each,
read its REQ-B and REQ-A bodies and record `change type` and behavior `before → after` (concrete values,
conditions, parameters). For `layout` changes list members/enum values whose offset or value shifts.

### B2 – Anchor every request item in latest source (graph-driven loop)
Goal: for every node of `_work/A_links.md` (and so every S-id and file), find where it lives **now** in
`SOURCE_ROOT`, even when files or names changed. Names are searched first, then content, then relations;
every anchor records the method and the signals (R12 confidence rules).

**B2.0 – Prepare.** Write `_work/B_feature_ids.txt` = names of the `medium`/`volatile` nodes (one per line; used by
R16/R17). Order the nodes: `stable` → `medium` → `volatile`; inside a class, nodes with more edges first.

**B2.1 – Files.** Same path exists in `SOURCE_ROOT`? If not → R11 (basename, includes/builds links, content,
R17 fallback). Result: `SAME_PATH` / `MOVED_FILE <new path>` / `SPLIT_FILE <paths>` / `NOT_FOUND`.

**B2.2 – Nodes, one pass in B2.0 order.** For each not-yet-anchored node:
1. Exact name (R2) in the anchored file(s), then repo-wide. Found → **verify it is the same thing**: same kind,
   body comparable (R7 or R17 `blind` ≥ 0.6 against REQ-A), and not a different `static` symbol with the same name.
   Verified → `SAME_NAME` / `MOVED_SYMBOL` (method `NAME`, confidence `High`). Name found but body unrelated →
   treat as not found (name reused) and note it.
2. Not found by name → climb the R12 ladder: L0 alias → L1 walk the links (only edges whose other end is anchored)
   → L2 fuzzy lines (R16) → L3 stable anchors → L4 similarity (R17) → L5 rename pattern → L6 hypotheses.
   Result: `RENAMED_SYMBOL <new name>` / `SPLIT_SYMBOL` / `MERGED_SYMBOL` with method(s), signals, confidence.
3. Still nothing → leave it for the next iteration (a neighbor anchored later may unlock it).
Every new rename/move goes into `_work/alias_map.md` immediately (`request → latest`, method, signals); every
consistent rename rule found goes in as `kind = pattern` (R12 L5).

**B2.3 – Cross-check through the links.** For each edge whose both ends are now anchored, check that the latest
code still shows the relation with the latest names (e.g. request `A calls B`, alias `B → B'` ⇒ latest body of
`A'` calls `B'`; table entry of ID still points to the handler's latest name). Result per edge:
`consistent` / `changed (<what>)` / `broken`. A `broken` edge downgrades the less certain end one level (R12) and
is listed as a risk; `changed` is normal evolution (B3 will classify it).

**B2.4 – Iterate.** Repeat B2.2–B2.3 for the nodes still open. Stop when an iteration anchors no new node.
Log each iteration in `_work/B_anchor.md`: `Iteration k: +n anchored (NAME a, EDGE e, FUZZY f, ANCHOR c, SIM s, PATTERN p)`.

**B2.5 – Still not found → eliminate (R12 L7).** For each remaining node record which checks were run and conclude
`MACRO_GENERATED <macro, SRC:path:line>` / `REWRITTEN` (anchors present, structure gone) / `NOT_FOUND (removed)` /
`NOT_FOUND (unknown)`. Encoding mismatches must be ruled out before `NOT_FOUND`.

**B2.6 – Latest state and hunks (modulo aliases).** Only now, with the alias map complete:
- Apply the alias map to the request text first: in REQ-A bodies and `+` lines, replace every request name by its
  latest name (`_work/B_aliased/<path>`; never edit the inputs). Whole words only, longest names first, e.g.
  `LC_ALL=C sed -E 's/(^|[^A-Za-z0-9_])OLD([^A-Za-z0-9_]|$)/\1NEW\2/g'` (portable BSD/GNU; run twice for adjacent hits).
- Compare the aliased REQ-A body with the latest body (R7): `UNCHANGED_IN_LATEST` / `EVOLVED` / `REMOVED_IN_LATEST`.
- Per hunk: each distinctive aliased `+` line found in the anchored latest body (`grep -F`, then R16 for lines that
  still miss) → `PRESENT` (all found), `PARTIAL`, `GONE`. Lines found only after aliasing or only by R16 are marked
  `(modulo aliases)` / `(fuzzy)` with the matching `SRC:path:line`.
- Write `_work/B_anchor.md`.
Any `NOT_FOUND`, `REWRITTEN`, `MACRO_GENERATED`, `REMOVED_IN_LATEST`, `GONE`, `broken` edge or `Low` anchor →
blocker with a question.

### B3 – Classify later evolution (only `EVOLVED` items)
Diff the **aliased** REQ-A body (`_work/B_aliased/`, B2.6) against the latest body, so pure renames do not show up
as change blocks (a rename-only difference is `REFACTOR`). For each later change block apply R14:
`EXTENSION` (feature grew: related to feature tokens/lines/guard), `REFACTOR` (rename/format/move of
feature lines), `BUGFIX` (fix to feature lines), `UNRELATED` (another feature or unrelated refactor in the
same function), `UNCLEAR`. Record per block with `SRC:path:line`. `UNCLEAR` → blocker.

### B4 – Discover feature extensions outside the request's symbols
The feature may have grown into new places after the request. Search latest source **with the latest names**
(alias map), never only with the request names – after a rename the old names find nothing:
- every use of the feature's symbols/macros/strings (latest names) outside the anchored symbols (R3),
- code under the feature's guard macro(s) (R5 inverse: `grep -n "<GUARD>"` then read the blocks),
- symbols with the feature's naming prefix – the request prefix **and** every latest prefix from `alias_map.md`
  `kind = pattern` rows (`grep -rnw -E "<Prefix>[A-Za-z0-9_]*"`), new files referencing them,
- the stable anchors of the feature (string IDs, NVRAM keys, command keywords from `A_links.md`) in places not yet anchored.
Classify each hit: `EXTENSION_NEW` (belongs to the feature itself: inside its guard, in its files, named with its
prefix, or only reachable from the feature) / `CONSUMER` (another feature uses this one → `REPORT_ONLY` later) /
`UNCLEAR` (blocker). `EXTENSION_NEW` items get new S-ids marked `ext`.

### B5 – Port version and outgoing closure (code + data)
*Port version* of each S = latest body restricted to: request lines + `EXTENSION`/`REFACTOR`/`BUGFIX`
blocks (exclude `UNRELATED`). Note when the latest body mixes in `UNRELATED` blocks: partial take.
1. R4 on the port version text (request `+` lines **and** extension lines from latest) → `_work/B_new_tokens.txt`.
2. For each project token: is it an S-id? Otherwise find its definition in `SOURCE_ROOT` latest (R2) → dependency
   `S###.d#` with kind and `SRC:path:line`.
3. **Data dependencies** (R13): string IDs + every language table entry, enum entries + all arrays indexed or
   sized by that enum, settings/NVRAM fields + default tables + reset/init + version/migration/checksum,
   registry/menu/command/event table entries, resource/data/config files (search **all** file types), build entries.
4. Recurse into each dependency's body (R1 + R4 on its range). Stop rule here: generic infrastructure
   (used by > ~10 unrelated files, record it) or nothing new. Final stop against the target is done in C (fixpoint).
5. Headers (R6) and guards (R5) for every ported line; where each guard macro is enabled in source.

### B6 – Incoming dependencies needed for behavior
For each S (request + `ext`): callers and non-call uses (R3) → `needed-for-behavior` (registration entry,
init call, default value, dispatcher case) or `CONSUMER`.

### B7 – Tests
R9: tests touching each S, or `none found (patterns)`.

### B8 – Write the report
- `### Files Analyzed`: every manifest file → `analyzed` / `skipped (reason)`.
- `### Latest Source Anchoring`: `| H/S-id | request location | latest location | anchor result | latest state | method | evidence (signals) | confidence |`
  + alias map entries (incl. rename patterns) + iteration log + link cross-check counts (`consistent / changed / broken`)
  + `#### Anchored Link Graph`: the A7 graph coloured by anchor result, with the latest name of every node, so the
  reviewer sees how anchors propagated (paste the output, without the edge table already shown in A):
  `python3 -I "$SK/scripts/links_view.py" --links "$W/A_links.md" --anchor "$W/B_anchor.md" --no-table --out "$W/B_links.mmd"`.
- `### Changed Symbols and Behavior`: `| S-id | symbol (kind) | H-ids / ext | change type | behavior before → after | later evolution |`.
- `### Dependencies and Test Coverage`: outgoing code deps, data deps, incoming deps, guards, headers, tests.
- `### Blockers and Context Risk`: unresolved anchors, UNCLEAR evolution/extension, partial takes, macro-generated
  code, runtime-assigned function pointers, complex `#if`, layout changes.
Run `gates/B.md`, write `### Gate Result`, update Workflow Status.

## Stop message
```
Checkpoint B <Complete|Blocked>.
Anchoring: same a · moved m · renamed r · split/merged s · not found n · evolved e · removed x
Methods: NAME a · EDGE e · FUZZY f · ANCHOR c · SIM s · PATTERN p · LLM-led l · iterations k · broken links: <list or none>
Rename patterns: <request → latest rules or none>
Extensions found: <k> (new symbols <list>) · Consumers (report only): <list>

# Checkpoint B – Source Change Analysis (anchor in latest source + feature closure)

**Goal:** starting from the request diff, trace back into `SOURCE_ROOT` (latest source), find where
every piece of the request lives *now* (even if files or functions were moved or renamed), find how the
feature was **extended** after the request, and collect the full closure of code **and data** the feature
needs. The result is the *port version* of the feature: what will be merged to the target.
**Reads:** `_work/A_hunks.md`, `_work/A_links.md`, `diffs/source/**`, `SOURCE_REQUEST/Before|After`, `SOURCE_ROOT` (search and
narrow reads; plain folder, no history – everything is inferred from content).
**Writes:** `_work/B_feature_ids.txt`, `_work/B_aliased/**`, `_work/B_anchor.md`, `_work/alias_map.md`, `_work/B_new_tokens.txt`,
`_work/B_symbols.md`, report section B.
**Load:** `references/c-cpp-search-recipes.md` (R1–R7, R9, R11–R17), `references/glossary.md`; uses `_work/A_links.md`.

## Steps

### B1 – Changed symbols (request view)
From `_work/A_hunks.md` create one `S###` per distinct symbol (several H-ids may share one S). For each,
read its REQ-B and REQ-A bodies and record `change type` and behavior `before → after` (concrete values,
conditions, parameters). For `layout` changes list members/enum values whose offset or value shifts.

### B2 – Anchor every request item in latest source (graph-driven loop)
Goal: for every node of `_work/A_links.md` (and so every S-id and file), find where it lives **now** in
`SOURCE_ROOT`, even when files or names changed. Names are searched first, then content, then relations;
every anchor records the method and the signals (R12 confidence rules).

**B2.0 – Prepare.** Write `_work/B_feature_ids.txt` = names of the `medium`/`volatile` nodes (one per line; used by
R16/R17). Order the nodes: `stable` → `medium` → `volatile`; inside a class, nodes with more edges first.

**B2.1 – Files.** Same path exists in `SOURCE_ROOT`? If not → R11 (basename, includes/builds links, content,
R17 fallback). Result: `SAME_PATH` / `MOVED_FILE <new path>` / `SPLIT_FILE <paths>` / `NOT_FOUND`.

**B2.2 – Nodes, one pass in B2.0 order.** For each not-yet-anchored node:
1. Exact name (R2) in the anchored file(s), then repo-wide. Found → **verify it is the same thing**: same kind,
   body comparable (R7 or R17 `blind` ≥ 0.6 against REQ-A), and not a different `static` symbol with the same name.
   Verified → `SAME_NAME` / `MOVED_SYMBOL` (method `NAME`, confidence `High`). Name found but body unrelated →
   treat as not found (name reused) and note it.
2. Not found by name → climb the R12 ladder: L0 alias → L1 walk the links (only edges whose other end is anchored)
   → L2 fuzzy lines (R16) → L3 stable anchors → L4 similarity (R17) → L5 rename pattern → L6 hypotheses.
   Result: `RENAMED_SYMBOL <new name>` / `SPLIT_SYMBOL` / `MERGED_SYMBOL` with method(s), signals, confidence.
3. Still nothing → leave it for the next iteration (a neighbor anchored later may unlock it).
Every new rename/move goes into `_work/alias_map.md` immediately (`request → latest`, method, signals); every
consistent rename rule found goes in as `kind = pattern` (R12 L5).

**B2.3 – Cross-check through the links.** For each edge whose both ends are now anchored, check that the latest
code still shows the relation with the latest names (e.g. request `A calls B`, alias `B → B'` ⇒ latest body of
`A'` calls `B'`; table entry of ID still points to the handler's latest name). Result per edge:
`consistent` / `changed (<what>)` / `broken`. A `broken` edge downgrades the less certain end one level (R12) and
is listed as a risk; `changed` is normal evolution (B3 will classify it).

**B2.4 – Iterate.** Repeat B2.2–B2.3 for the nodes still open. Stop when an iteration anchors no new node.
Log each iteration in `_work/B_anchor.md`: `Iteration k: +n anchored (NAME a, EDGE e, FUZZY f, ANCHOR c, SIM s, PATTERN p)`.

**B2.5 – Still not found → eliminate (R12 L7).** For each remaining node record which checks were run and conclude
`MACRO_GENERATED <macro, SRC:path:line>` / `REWRITTEN` (anchors present, structure gone) / `NOT_FOUND (removed)` /
`NOT_FOUND (unknown)`. Encoding mismatches must be ruled out before `NOT_FOUND`.

**B2.6 – Latest state and hunks (modulo aliases).** Only now, with the alias map complete:
- Apply the alias map to the request text first: in REQ-A bodies and `+` lines, replace every request name by its
  latest name (`_work/B_aliased/<path>`; never edit the inputs). Whole words only, longest names first, e.g.
  `LC_ALL=C sed -E 's/(^|[^A-Za-z0-9_])OLD([^A-Za-z0-9_]|$)/\1NEW\2/g'` (portable BSD/GNU; run twice for adjacent hits).
- Compare the aliased REQ-A body with the latest body (R7): `UNCHANGED_IN_LATEST` / `EVOLVED` / `REMOVED_IN_LATEST`.
- Per hunk: each distinctive aliased `+` line found in the anchored latest body (`grep -F`, then R16 for lines that
  still miss) → `PRESENT` (all found), `PARTIAL`, `GONE`. Lines found only after aliasing or only by R16 are marked
  `(modulo aliases)` / `(fuzzy)` with the matching `SRC:path:line`.
- Write `_work/B_anchor.md`.
Any `NOT_FOUND`, `REWRITTEN`, `MACRO_GENERATED`, `REMOVED_IN_LATEST`, `GONE`, `broken` edge or `Low` anchor →
blocker with a question.

### B3 – Classify later evolution (only `EVOLVED` items)
Diff the **aliased** REQ-A body (`_work/B_aliased/`, B2.6) against the latest body, so pure renames do not show up
as change blocks (a rename-only difference is `REFACTOR`). For each later change block apply R14:
`EXTENSION` (feature grew: related to feature tokens/lines/guard), `REFACTOR` (rename/format/move of
feature lines), `BUGFIX` (fix to feature lines), `UNRELATED` (another feature or unrelated refactor in the
same function), `UNCLEAR`. Record per block with `SRC:path:line`. `UNCLEAR` → blocker.

### B4 – Discover feature extensions outside the request's symbols
The feature may have grown into new places after the request. Search latest source **with the latest names**
(alias map), never only with the request names – after a rename the old names find nothing:
- every use of the feature's symbols/macros/strings (latest names) outside the anchored symbols (R3),
- code under the feature's guard macro(s) (R5 inverse: `grep -n "<GUARD>"` then read the blocks),
- symbols with the feature's naming prefix – the request prefix **and** every latest prefix from `alias_map.md`
  `kind = pattern` rows (`grep -rnw -E "<Prefix>[A-Za-z0-9_]*"`), new files referencing them,
- the stable anchors of the feature (string IDs, NVRAM keys, command keywords from `A_links.md`) in places not yet anchored.
Classify each hit: `EXTENSION_NEW` (belongs to the feature itself: inside its guard, in its files, named with its
prefix, or only reachable from the feature) / `CONSUMER` (another feature uses this one → `REPORT_ONLY` later) /
`UNCLEAR` (blocker). `EXTENSION_NEW` items get new S-ids marked `ext`.

*Port version* of each S = latest body restricted to: request lines + `EXTENSION`/`REFACTOR`/`BUGFIX`
blocks (exclude `UNRELATED`). Note when the latest body mixes in `UNRELATED` blocks: partial take.

2. For each project token: is it an S-id? Otherwise find its definition in `SOURCE_ROOT` latest (R2) → dependency
   `S###.d#` with kind and `SRC:path:line`.
3. **Data dependencies** (R13): string IDs + every language table entry, enum entries + all arrays indexed or
   sized by that enum, settings/NVRAM fields + default tables + reset/init + version/migration/checksum,
   registry/menu/command/event table entries, resource/data/config files (search **all** file types), build entries.
4. Recurse into each dependency's body (R1 + R4 on its range). Stop rule here: generic infrastructure
   (used by > ~10 unrelated files, record it) or nothing new. Final stop against the target is done in C (fixpoint).
5. Headers (R6) and guards (R5) for every ported line; where each guard macro is enabled in source.

### B6 – Incoming dependencies needed for behavior
For each S (request + `ext`): callers and non-call uses (R3) → `needed-for-behavior` (registration entry,
init call, default value, dispatcher case) or `CONSUMER`.

### B7 – Tests
R9: tests touching each S, or `none found (patterns)`.

### B8 – Write the report
- `### Files Analyzed`: every manifest file → `analyzed` / `skipped (reason)`.
- `### Latest Source Anchoring`: `| H/S-id | request location | latest location | anchor result | latest state | method | evidence (signals) | confidence |`

- `### Changed Symbols and Behavior`: `| S-id | symbol (kind) | H-ids / ext | change type | behavior before → after | later evolution |`.
- `### Dependencies and Test Coverage`: outgoing code deps, data deps, incoming deps, guards, headers, tests.
- `### Blockers and Context Risk`: unresolved anchors, UNCLEAR evolution/extension, partial takes, macro-generated
  code, runtime-assigned function pointers, complex `#if`, layout changes.

# Checkpoint E – Before/After Implementation **Goal:** create the output snapshots and apply exactly the approved plan to `After/` – nothing more. **Reads:** `_work/D_plan.md`, `TARGET_ROOT` (copy source), `SOURCE_REQUEST/After`, `SOURCE_ROOT` (content sources). **Writes:** `OUTPUT_ROOT/Before/`, `OUTPUT_ROOT/After/`, `diffs/output.diff`, `_work/E_changes.md`, report section E. **Does not build or run tests** (that is F). Structural self-checks below are allowed. ## Steps ### E1 – Snapshots If D said existing snapshots will be replaced, delete only `OUTPUT_ROOT/Before` and `OUTPUT_ROOT/After` (verify the paths start with `OUTPUT_ROOT` before deleting). Then: ```bash rsync -a --exclude='.git' "$TARGET_ROOT"/ "$OUTPUT_ROOT/Before"/ rsync -a --exclude='.git' "$TARGET_ROOT"/ "$OUTPUT_ROOT/After"/ diff -rq "$TARGET_ROOT" "$OUTPUT_ROOT/Before" -x .git && echo BEFORE_IDENTICAL ``` Never edit `Before/` after this point. ### E2 – Apply planned changes, in P-id order For each P-id, edit only the file under `OUTPUT_ROOT/After/`: - Locate the anchor text exactly. If it is not found exactly once → do not improvise: mark the P `skipped (anchor not found)` and add a blocker. - Insert/replace with the full new text from `_work/D_plan.md`, verbatim (plus the D2 label if any). - `ADAPT_MERGE` (and optionally `APPLY_PORT_VERSION`): symbol-level 3-way merge – ```bash # base = REQ-B body, ours = target body (from After/), theirs = port version (from D_plan), each extracted to _work/merge/ git merge-file -p _work/merge/ours.txt _work/merge/base.txt _work/merge/theirs.txt > _work/merge/result.txt; echo "conflicts=$?" ``` `git merge-file` needs no repository. Do **not** substitute `diff3 -m` (wrong merges on macOS). Without `git`: apply the planned anchor-based edit; if any anchor of the request lines is missing in the target body → treat as conflict. `conflicts=0` → put `result.txt` in place of the target body. `>0` → do not hand-resolve silently: mark the P `skipped (merge conflict)` + blocker (interactive: show the conflict and ask). - `add-file`: copy the file from the content source byte-for-byte (`cp -p`), then apply other P-ids to it if planned. - Preserve encoding and line endings: check `file -I` before/after the edit; for non-UTF-8 files edit via `iconv` into `_work/`, edit, convert back, and confirm with `file -I` and a diff that only planned lines changed. - Record `E###` in `_work/E_changes.md` with resulting `OUT-A:path:lines`. ### E3 – Output diff and self-check ```bash cd "$OUTPUT_ROOT" && git diff --no-index --no-color -U3 Before After > diffs/output.diff; git diff --no-index --stat Before After # without git: diff -ruN Before After > diffs/output.diff; diff -rq Before After ``` Map every hunk of `diffs/output.diff` to an E-id. A hunk with no E-id = unplanned change → revert it. A P-id with no hunk (and not `skipped`) = not applied → fix. ### E4 – Write the report - D's section is frozen (never edit it). First line of `### Exact Changes`: `Executing plan approved by: `. - `### Output File Manifest`, `### Exact Changes` (formats in `report-template.md`). - `### Diff Summary`: `--stat` totals + one line per file. - `### Blockers`: skipped P-ids, encoding issues, anything that deviated. Run `gates/E.md`, write `### Gate Result`, update Workflow Status. ## Stop message ``` Checkpoint E . Snapshots: Before (identical to target: yes) · After: files changed, +/- lines Applied: /

P-ids · Skipped: · Unplanned hunks: 0 Output diff: /diffs/output.diff Reply "approve F" to validate and hand off. ``` # Gate E 1. **Before identical** – `diff -rq -x .git "$TARGET_ROOT" "$OUTPUT_ROOT/Before"` prints nothing. 2. **Every P applied** – every P-id has exactly one E-id with status `applied`, or `skipped` + reason + blocker. 3. **No unplanned change** – every hunk in `diffs/output.diff` maps to an E-id (show hunk count vs mapped count). 4. **Files** – set of files in `git diff --no-index --name-only Before After` (or `diff -rq Before After`) == files in `### Output File Manifest`. 5. **Verbatim** – for E-ids with adaptation `none`, the inserted text equals the D text (`diff -w` on the extracted lines). 6. **Encoding / EOL** – `file -I` and CRLF status of every modified file are unchanged versus `Before/`. 7. **Labels** – applied only if D found a convention, in exactly that format. 8. **No validation run** – no build/test commands were executed in E. 9. **Read-only inputs** – marker check on `SOURCE_ROOT`, `TARGET_ROOT`, `SOURCE_REQUEST` prints nothing. 10. **Status row** updated. # Checkpoint F – Validation and Handoff **Goal:** prove the port builds/works as far as the project allows, prove that only approved changes exist, prove inputs were not modified, and hand off clearly. **Reads:** `OUTPUT_ROOT/Before|After`, all `_work` files, the report. **Writes:** `_work/F_validation.md`, build artifacts only inside `OUTPUT_ROOT/Before|After`, report section F. ## Steps ### F1 – Determine the command Use `BUILD_CMD` or the command from D's Validation Plan. If it is still unclear (several candidates, needs toolchain/env you cannot confirm): interactive → ask before running and before claiming success; auto → run the best candidate and label the result `UNCONFIRMED COMMAND`. ### F2 – Baseline and validation runs Run the same command in `OUTPUT_ROOT/Before` (baseline) and `OUTPUT_ROOT/After`. Save trimmed output (command, exit code, last ~40 lines, every error/warning line mentioning a ported file) to `_work/F_validation.md`. - After fails but Before passes → port problem: analyse the errors, map missing symbols with R2/R3. Fixes are **not** made silently: interactive → propose and ask (approved fixes get new ids `P-F#`/`E-F#`, are applied to `After/` only, and are listed in F's Validation section; D/E sections stay frozen); auto → at most 2 fix rounds restricted to plan-consistent fixes (missing include/declaration/dependency copy), each flagged `AUTO-DECIDED`. - Both fail the same way → environment/pre-existing issue; do not claim validation, record it. - No build possible → fallback from D (`-fsyntax-only` per changed file with include paths, symbol resolution greps). Label clearly as `partial validation`. Run related tests found in B7 if runnable. ### F3 – Before/After comparison Regenerate `diffs/output.diff`; confirm it equals E's version (no change since E). Confirm every hunk maps to an E-id and every E-id to an approved P-id. ### F4 – Traceability Build `### Traceability Matrix`: one row per H-id, per `ext` S-id and per dependency S###.d# (code and data): H → S → M → P → E → output hunk → result (`ported`, `ported (ext)`, `already present`, `skipped: `, `report only`, `blocked`). No empty cell without a reason. ### F5 – Input integrity ```bash (cd "$SOURCE_REQUEST" && find Before After -type f -exec shasum {} +) | diff - "$OUTPUT_ROOT/_work/input_baseline.txt" && echo REQUEST_UNCHANGED find "$SOURCE_ROOT" "$TARGET_ROOT" -newer "$OUTPUT_ROOT/_work/.start_marker" -type f -not -path '*/.git/*' | head ``` The second command must print nothing (if it prints files, report them – they may be changes by someone else; do not claim integrity). ### F6 – Write the report - `### Validation Commands and Results`: `| Where | Command | Exit | Result |` + key error lines. - `### Before/After Comparison`: F3 result. - `### Traceability Matrix`. - `### Limitations and Tests Not Run`: everything not validated and why, `partial validation`, `UNCONFIRMED COMMAND`. - `### Final Handoff`: output paths (`OUTPUT_ROOT`, `After/`, `diffs/output.diff`, report), validation status (`Validated` / `Partially validated` / `Not validated`), decisions for human review (CONFLICT choices, AUTO-DECIDED items, ENABLE_GUARD, LAYOUT_RISK, drift, REPORT_ONLY list), next steps. Run `gates/F.md`, write `### Gate Result`, update Workflow Status (F → `Complete`, next gate `None`). ## Final message ``` Port : After: · Diff: · Report: Build: Before / After · Tests: Traceability: hunks → ported p, already present a, skipped s, report-only r, blocked b Needs human review: ``` # Gate F 1. **Commands recorded** – every validation command with directory, exit code and result; Before baseline included. 2. **Honest status** – `Validated` only if After build (and runnable tests) succeeded with a confirmed command; otherwise `Partially validated` / `Not validated` with reasons. 3. **Diff stable** – `diffs/output.diff` matches the E version, except approved `E-F#` fixes, which are listed. 4. **Traceability complete** – every H-id and dependency has a full row; no blank cell without a reason; counts per result type shown. 5. **Only approved changes** – every output hunk → E-id → approved P-id (or approved `P-F#`). 6. **Input integrity** – `REQUEST_UNCHANGED` printed and the `-newer` check printed nothing (or the files are reported). 7. **Handoff** – paths, validation status, human-review list (CONFLICT, AUTO-DECIDED, ENABLE_GUARD, LAYOUT_RISK, drift, REPORT_ONLY), limitations, tests not run. 8. **Single report** – only one `PORT_REPORT.md` under `OUTPUT_ROOT` (`find "$OUTPUT_ROOT" -name '*REPORT*'`); Run Metadata `REPORT_PATH` / `Created at` unchanged. 9. **Status row** – F = `Complete`, Next approval gate = `None`.

**Build and smoke run** (`make -s MODEL=B`):
- **Before (unmodified target):** builds with no warnings. The program prints `toner_save=-1 pjl=-1 density=10`, meaning the feature is absent.
- **After (ported):** builds with no `-Wall` warnings. It prints `toner_save=2 pjl=1 density=8`: the menu entry, the PJL command and density scaling all work. The target's own fax behaviour still works.
- Neither codebase has unit tests, so the build plus this smoke run is all the validation there is.

**What was ported:** 15 files changed (4 new, 11 modified), +92/−4 lines.
- All 13 request hunks were ported. None was skipped or blocked.
- The latest source has one later fix to the feature (`fix #1234`, which clamps the level). It was ported too, since your manual ports include post-request fixes.
- The feature needs `Density_Scale`, which lives in `density.c/.h`. The target doesn't have those files, so I copied them and added `density.c` to the Makefile.
- In six target files that already had their own changes (the fax feature), the request lines were merged in. `git merge-file` found no conflicts, and the fax code is kept.
- The feature switch went into `config/model_b.h`, the target's equivalent of the source's `config/model_a.h`.
- No input folder was modified.

**For human review** (decisions made automatically in auto mode):
1. **Saved settings layout:** `toner_save_level` is inserted in the middle of the settings struct that is stored in NVRAM (non-volatile memory). The later fields (`language`, `quality`, `fax_resolution`) move by 4 bytes, and the target has no version or migration code. Settings saved by older firmware would be read wrongly.
2. **Eco Report left out:** the latest source also has an Eco Report feature that uses toner save. It is a separate feature with its own on/off switch, so it was not ported. That covers its menu entry, include, Makefile line and switch define.
3. **Feature switch:** `#define SUPPORT_TONER_SAVE 1` was added to the end of `config/model_b.h`.
4. **`Clamp` signature replaced:** the target's 2-argument `Clamp(v, hi)` became the source's `Clamp(v, lo, hi)`. Nothing in the target calls it, so no existing behaviour changes.
5. **String ID shift:** adding the new string ID moves `STR_QUALITY` from 2 to 3 and `STR_FAX` from 3 to 4. These IDs are only used internally, not saved.

- `PORT_REPORT.md`
